rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ethyl vanillin production started after about 2 months of conversion with a 600-tonne ethyl campaign planned, but this is a product switch from methyl rather than a new molecule, and Vinpai and Vitafor are existing Blends businesses.

rows.label: Debt repayment and funding of about INR670 crores
rows.why: Debt ended FY26 at about INR670 crores with INR60-70 crores of repayments due in FY27, and management is pursuing structured or bank debt with equity as a last resort, while the CFS Europe liquidation removes INR50-60 crores of annual cash burn from next quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term Blends and vanillin demand and held FY27 guidance, but cautious on near-term margins, logistics and Q1 EBITDA, and was evasive on the cost of structured debt; analysts pushed on the Q1 EBITDA outlook, debt funding and the vanillin cost base.

532834|2026-06.headline: Camlin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR5,199 million, but EBITDA margin collapsed to about 4% from 45% last quarter on raw material costs and vanillin under-utilisation.
532834|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR5,199 million, up about 28% YoY and about INR1,000 million QoQ, but margins fell sharply on raw material, freight and logistics costs tied to the West Asia conflict. The company reorganised reporting into Specialty Ingredients, Aroma and Performance Chemicals, with Aroma and Performance Chemicals both EBITDA-negative or near zero in the quarter. Ethyl vanillin ramp-up ran at low utilisation, and FY27 vanillin volume guidance was cut to about 3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons. Management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 10-12% while keeping revenue guidance, and debt was flat at about INR640 crore gross.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients (blends and straights)
segments.commentary: Revenue above INR4,000 million with blends above INR3,000 million; EBITDA margin 6.35%. Management says about 4-5% of gross margin was lost to raw material costs and Brazil air-freight, with Brazil's shortfall of about INR8 crore expected to correct in Q2.

segments.name: Aroma (vanillin)
segments.commentary: Sold about 560 tons (350 t ethyl, 200 t methyl from channel stock) against 6,000-ton capacity; produced ~400 tons. Quarterly EBITDA negative at INR4-4.5 crore on fixed cost absorption; management expects positive EBITDA in Q2.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals
segments.commentary: Gross segment revenue about INR175 crore, of which ~INR130 crore is internal transfer, leaving ~INR40 crore external sales. EBITDA margin 2.5% with diphenol plant shut; management expects positive EBITDA from Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: INR2,200-2,300 crore, versus earlier INR2,000-2,400 crore; management says top line is secure.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 10-12% (10-11% per CFO/MD), implying about INR220-230 crore EBITDA, versus earlier INR250-280 crore.
Analyst read-back: average run rate of about INR70 crore EBITDA per quarter for remaining quarters; management did not dispute this.
Q3 FY27 expected to return to double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin; H2 margin of 13-15% floated by an analyst, not disputed.
FY28 EBITDA margin in the range of 12-14%.
Vanillin FY27 volume about 3,000 tons (earlier 3,600-4,000); 4 campaigns planned, Q2 volume 500-600 tons, Q3 1,000+ tons. Capacity 6,000 tons, achievable 5,000 tons with 3 campaigns.
Blends growth of at least 20% in FY27; budget assumes 25-30%.
capex_capacity: Vanillin capacity 6,000 tons per year; ethyl vanillin campaign of about 750 tons ran through mid-August, with about 350 tons sold and over 300 tons produced; methyl vanillin campaign to follow after roughly two weeks of changeover.
Diphenol plant shut because phenol and raw material prices are high; hydroquinone secured from China for the next two quarters; decision on alternate use or restart by Q3 FY27.
Working capital cycle about 100 days on a consolidated basis; each INR1 crore of revenue growth needs about one-third as working capital support.
CFS Europe in liquidation with no further cash burn beyond legal costs; China subsidiary liquidation expected to cost INR10-20 million in Q1.
demand_pricing: Channel stocks in the US and China described as cleared; management sees demand picking up and is negotiating quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts with F&F customers.
US and Europe ethyl vanillin realisations stated at about $13-14/kg; methyl vanillin raw material cost $7-8/kg, with conversion cost about INR7 crore/month fixed.
Management sees a supply gap of about 5,000-6,000 tons in US and Europe that must be imported; Syensqo (Solvay) is the market leader; Chinese imports priced around $15 against Solvay's $18.
Pass-through of raw material increases to blends customers is lagging by one quarter; management expects to recover about half of the cost increase in Q2.
Trade financing (dealer finance) on purchase and sales sides costs an estimated 1-1.5% and is hitting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA guidance achievable given Q1 EBITDA of about INR9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated guidance as INR2,200-2,300 crore revenue with 10-11% margin, which it said is within reach on the current cost structure; it expects about 10% margin over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Aroma EBITDA negative and what is its normalised economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low utilisation (about 400 tons produced vs 1,500-ton quarterly capacity) left fixed cost unabsorbed. Management said 70-80% utilisation would make the business profitable and gave about 7% EBITDA at $13/kg on 3,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt reduction and what external funding is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR640 crore, down from INR670 crore on 31 March. The CFO said INR100-200 crore of working capital lines are expected within 1-1.5 months, and equity or other capital is being considered without a decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 vanillin volume cut from 3,600-4,000 tons to about 3,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The ethyl vanillin ramp-up was slower to secure quality, with 95% customer approval. Each campaign switch costs about a month, and four campaigns are planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What would Q1 EBITDA have been under normal conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5% of gross margin was lost, which would have lifted EBITDA to roughly INR37-40 crore, an analyst's figure that management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost pressure persist into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects elevated raw material prices to persist through Q2 and guidance assumes about three months of elevated costs, not six or nine months.

The whole issue is on the margins.
So, on sales side, it's not a problem at all. The whole issue is on the purchase side.
Looking at the scenario, I think we will be able to just revisit these margins, and we feel that now the margin should be in the range of 10% to 12% this year.
Now, when the methyl vanillin starts, you will see that the margins will be significantly better, the gross margin.
The third is, of course, capital, which we are looking at different various options to be able to raise that capital.

532835|2026-03.headline: ICRA Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28.4% YoY, led by Research & Analytics (+56.8%) with Fintellix consolidated from October 2025.
532835|2026-03.overview: ICRA reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 28.4% YoY, with Research and Analytics up 56.8% on the Fintellix acquisition and Ratings up 10.6%. Q4 consolidated PBT before exceptional items and tax was INR 72.8 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 20.4% and PBT grew 10%, with exceptional charges from the new Labour Code excluded for comparability. Management flagged moderation in the Knowledge Services business and a margin-mix shift toward product-led businesses, and it sees near-term bond market softness offset by bank credit growth. Capital allocation questions (buyback, cash of over INR 700 crores, acquisition IRRs) were largely deflected, with the dividend raised and a special dividend declared.

segments.name: Ratings
segments.commentary: Revenue up 10.6% in Q4 and 14.2% for FY26. Management said the segment is a leverage play on economic activity, and Q4 growth was below some peers, which management attributed to a different base and strategic focus on growth segments.

segments.name: Research and Analytics
segments.commentary: Revenue up 56.8% in Q4 and 29.8% for FY26, driven by Fintellix (consolidated from October 2025, roughly 26% EBITDA margin per notes). Excluding Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly; Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily and turned profitable.

segments.name: Knowledge Services (KnowTech)
segments.commentary: Stable in core areas but growth moderated due to discontinued engagements and automation. Management expects a structural margin shift as non-KnowTech businesses, with different margin profiles, gain mix.

segments.name: Moody's-related non-ratings work
segments.commentary: Growth has been muted over the last couple of years and management expects moderation, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Some periodic in-sourcing by the parent continues.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance given; management cited a BankTech product-led EBITDA range of 20% to 35%, depending on geography mix.
Management expects Fintellix to drive reasonable growth over the next 2 to 3 years, partly offsetting Knowledge Services moderation, without quantifying it.
ICRA projects India GDP growth moderating to 6.2% in real terms in FY27, assuming average crude of $95 per barrel.

Management expects bank credit to drive most ratings growth in the near term, with bond market activity subdued due to higher yields; no significant slowdown seen in the first couple of months of FY27.
Bank transition to the expected credit loss framework from 1 April 2027 is expected to sustain demand for risk modelling and compliance solutions.
Management expects roughly INR 180 to 200 crores of cash flow generation in FY27, per an analyst's figure that management did not dispute.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Research and Analytics reorganised into KnowTech, BankTech and CapTech, supported by a unified IT and product engineering organisation.
Ongoing investment in analytics platforms, compliance capabilities and AI-powered agents; AI layer being integrated into subsidiary analytical tools.
demand_pricing: Ratings demand is tied to bank credit and bond issuance; the first couple of months of FY27 showed no significant slowdown, but geopolitical headwinds persist.
Fintellix competitors cited: Regnology and Nasdaq Technologies (global, PE or public-backed, acquisition-driven), plus system integrators and some Indian CRAs with risk and regulatory solutions.
About USD 18 million of FY26 revenue is dollar-denominated (roughly one-third of about INR 600 crores revenue, per management's figure); dollar-denominated costs are not significant.
Fintellix shift from one-time licence plus smaller recurring fee toward annuity or subscription model is in progress, but not all clients are ready to adopt it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Ratings growth materially lower than peers, and what is the non-ratings growth ex-Fintellix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ICRA is in a similar band to peers, with double-digit growth over the last 4 years, and that growth-segment focus is the strategy. Ex-Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly while Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration given over INR 700 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a rising dividend (normal dividend INR 60 to INR 70 per share plus special dividend) and said alternative capital allocation options are being evaluated, subject to Board approval and tax changes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ratings outlook for FY27, and what are April-May borrowing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bond activity to stay subdued given higher yields, with bank credit driving growth. No significant slowdown was seen in the first couple of months of FY27. No revenue growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&A margins evolve as the mix shifts, and could Ratings margins exceed 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said product-led BankTech-type businesses earn 20% to 35% EBITDA margins, and that double-digit Ratings revenue growth typically brings margin expansion as employee cost growth stays below 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Moody's-related work and in-sourcing from the parent?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth has been muted and is expected to moderate, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Periodic in-sourcing continues, with new project work arriving on an ongoing basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fintellix segment profit and business description?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give Fintellix-specific contribution, citing parity of disclosure, but referred to notes to accounts showing around 26% EBITDA margin. Fintellix was described as RiskTech and RegTech, covering regulatory reporting and credit analytics for banks, insurers and asset managers.

risks_watch: Elevated energy prices from the West Asia conflict and a possible weak monsoon could weigh on FY27 growth and credit demand.
Knowledge Services growth moderation and automation trends could continue to pressure segment margins during the mix shift.
Limited disclosure of acquisition returns and Fintellix-specific financials, which shareholders have asked about.
Ratings margin gap versus other CRAs; management intends to close it through sales growth.
Capital allocation: whether cash above INR 700 crores is returned to shareholders via buyback or other means, pending Board decision.

rows.why: Management flagged Knowledge Services moderation, Moody's-related growth expected to moderate, and risks from elevated energy prices and possible weak monsoon, though no formal guidance exists to cut.

rows.label: Bank ECL transition sustaining risk-modelling demand
rows.why: Banks move to the expected credit loss framework from 1 April 2027, which management expects to sustain demand for risk modelling and compliance solutions, supporting Fintellix's ~26% EBITDA-margin business.

rows.label: Capital allocation: buyback or other returns on over INR 700 crore cash
rows.why: Management said alternative capital allocation options are being evaluated subject to Board approval and tax changes; a normal dividend rose from INR 60 to INR 70 plus a INR 35 special dividend, but no buyback was committed.

rows.label: Fintellix shift to annuity or subscription model
rows.why: Shift from one-time licence plus smaller recurring fee toward annuity/subscription is in progress, but not all clients are ready to adopt it, with no quantified timing.

tone.note: Management was confident on Ratings resilience (double-digit growth over four years) and the Fintellix platform, but cautious on bond markets and the macro outlook; analysts pushed on the buyback and cash above INR 700 crore, Fintellix-specific profit, acquisition IRRs and Ratings growth versus peer

532843|2026-03.headline: Fortis FY26 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR9,128 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 22.8%; FY27 guidance is 15%+ hospital revenue growth.
532843|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR9,128 crores (+17.3%), with hospital revenue up 19.1% to INR7,773 crores and consolidated operating EBITDA up 31.3% to INR2,085 crores (22.8% margin vs 20.4%). Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,365 crores (+17.8%) and PAT rose 44.2% to INR271 crores. Management flagged softer Q4 occupancy at several large hospitals, attributed to a drop in international patients and a government price cap on oncology drugs affecting CGHS/ECHS business in Punjab. Net debt rose to INR2,334 crores (1.09x net debt/EBITDA) on acquisitions and investments.

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR7,773 crores (+19.1%), operating EBITDA margin 22.2% vs 20.5%; ~85% of consolidated revenue and EBITDA. Q4 revenue INR2,023 crores (+19%), Q4 EBITDA margin 22.1%. Occupancy 68% vs 69%; ARPOB up 3.4% to INR2.51 crores.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue INR1,527 crores (+8.5%), operating EBITDA INR360 crores (23.6% margin vs 17.7%; 23.2% ex one-offs). Q4 gross revenue INR387 crores (+11.1%), EBITDA INR85 crores, margin 22%; Q4 tests ~10 million (+5%). Preventive health 13% of mix vs 11%; B2C:B2B 52:48 for FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital revenue growth guided at 15%+ on an ongoing (organic) basis; acquisitions excluded and additive.
FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 150 bps; long-term target of 25% by FY28 reaffirmed, with management seeing 1.5%-2% annual improvement.
Diagnostics FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23%-24%; revenue growth targeted at double digits (currently ~8.5%), with ~70% volume and ~30% value mix.
Jaipur expected to grow ~15% in FY27 with 13%-14% EBITDA margin.
Brownfield bed additions of 500+ in FY27 and ~1,800 beds over the next 4 years; capex about INR900 crores annually (about 60% maintenance).
Dividend of INR1 per share (10% of face value), fourth consecutive year, subject to shareholder approval.
IHH reportedly plans to raise stake to 50% and infuse ~INR10,000 crores fresh equity; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR700 crores; ~250 beds added via brownfield (Manesar, Noida, Faridabad) and ~800 beds added in total including acquisitions.

Acquired People Tree Hospital (125 beds, Bengaluru, Jan 2026) with land for 300+ beds; Shrimann Super Specialty Jalandhar (228 beds, Jul 2025) with land for 450+ beds; 200-bed Greater Noida lease (Sep 2025); Adayu 36-bed mental health facility in Gurugram (Nov 2025).
FMRI new tower to be operationalised within about a week, opening ~100 beds in FY27 on a phased basis; FY27 brownfield additions of 400+ beds per earlier statement, with 500+ per later remark.
Shalimar Bagh expansion delayed pending approvals; ~300 beds moved from FY28 to FY29; Mohali, Shalimar Bagh and Amritsar large towers ~2.5-3 years away.
BG Road has ~100 beds of brownfield capacity uncommissioned until occupancy improves; Mulund considering another tower.
demand_pricing: Hospital occupancy 68% in FY26 vs 69%; occupied beds up 15% (management cited 3,270 to 2,838, a figure order inverted in the transcript). FMRI at 85-95% occupancy; BG Road at ~55% vs ~63-64% area norm.
International patient revenue +18.5% to INR639 crores (7.8% of hospital revenue); Q4 international growth ~11%. Management is diversifying to Africa and other markets.
Oncology drug price capping (~30% of MRP) under CGHS/ECHS led Fortis to stop some high-cost drug cases, mainly in Punjab; no timeline for resolution. Management said margin impact is limited.
Focus specialties grew 18.9% and make up 62% of hospital revenue; radiation therapy volumes +19%, robotic surgeries +66%.
Diagnostics: 40.8 million tests in FY26 vs 39.2 million; 50+ new tests added; Illumina NovaSeq X operational at Mumbai reference lab.

qa_highlights.question: Why are occupancies falling at large hospitals such as FMRI and BG Road, and how will this improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal attributed the drop mainly to lower international business (Q4 growth ~11% vs 18-20% for the year) and oncology drug capping in Punjab. He said BG Road is low due to TPA/cash mix, intense competition and a 55% level versus a 63-64% area norm, with a target above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand given new capacity and doctor cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashutosh Raghuvanshi said doctor costs rose slightly but further increases are not expected; the 25% FY28 margin target is intact, with 1.5-2% annual improvement now seen as more confident.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did the 800 new beds contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Q4 hospital revenue of INR2,000 crores would be INR1,928 crores excluding People Tree, Adayu and Jalandhar, so new-unit contribution is small.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA of Gleneagles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not consolidate Gleneagles and does not track full-year numbers; it is trending around INR70 per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is Diagnostics demerger being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the focus is on profitability, this is not the time to lock value, and alternatives may be considered once the business matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Gleneagles transaction moving forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is under deliberation and evaluation; no timeline, and it would need majority-of-minority approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Manesar run-rate and FMRI ARPOB driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar FY26 revenue was INR140 crores at ~48% occupancy (new beds being added) and reached EBITDA breakeven. FMRI ARPOB rise was attributed to gross-basis international business, MR Linac, Gamma Knife and day-care oncology.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Jaipur and FEHI improving, and why build a Bangalore hospital in a competitive market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operational efficiency, new facilities and clinical talent at FEHI; Jaipur expected to grow ~15% at 13-14% margin. The People Tree site is a less competitive micro-market with underserved catchment, per Ashutosh Raghuvanshi.

risks_watch: Oncology drug price caps under CGHS/ECHS and the pace of revenue loss in Punjab, with no resolution timeline.
Occupancy at large hospitals (FMRI, BG Road, Faridabad) and absorption of new beds in Gurgaon and Noida amid doctor cost pressure.
International patient growth slowing (Q4 ~11%) and sustainability of domestic growth offsetting it.
Shalimar Bagh approval delays moving ~300 beds from FY28 to FY29.
Debt rise to 1.09x net debt/EBITDA after acquisitions; FY27 capex about INR900 crores.
Pending Gleneagles transaction and IHH equity infusion, both without timelines.
532843|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on full-year financials and FY27 guidance, reaffirming the 25% FY28 hospital margin target. Cautious and evasive on the oncology pricing issue, Gleneagles, IHH capital and some occupancy questions, giving no timelines or figures where they were requested.
key_quotes: If at all, we are more confident now that we can continue to deliver this progress every year, at least to 1.5% to 2% year-on-year.
So revenue-wise, we are well poised to see on hospital side, 15% plus revenue growth.
And I think this is not the right time to do any sort of value locking at this point.

rows.why: Management guides hospital EBITDA margin up about 150 bps in FY27 (FY26 hospital margin 22.2% vs 20.5%), with 25% FY28 target reaffirmed and 1.5-2% annual improvement seen; doctor cost increases not expected to rise further.

rows.why: Oncology drug price cap under CGHS/ECHS (~30% of MRP) in Punjab with no resolution timeline, softer Q4 occupancy at FMRI and BG Road (BG Road ~55% vs 63-64% area norm), and international growth slowing to ~11% in Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Diagnostics added 50+ new tests in FY26 and Illumina NovaSeq X is operational at Mumbai; no specific new hospital or product launch date was guided.

rows.label: Gleneagles transaction and IHH equity infusion
rows.why: Gleneagles is under deliberation with no timeline and needs majority-of-minority approval; IHH reportedly plans to raise stake to 50% with ~INR10,000 crores fresh equity, unconfirmed by management.

rows.label: International patient growth and Africa diversification
rows.why: International revenue rose 18.5% to INR639 crores (7.8% of hospital revenue) in FY26, but Q4 growth slowed to ~11%, and management is diversifying into Africa and other markets.

532843|2026-06.headline: Fortis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.5% to INR 2,545 crore, but hospital EBITDA margin slipped to 21.5% from 22.1% on ESOP, ramp-up and legal costs.
532843|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17.5% YoY to INR 2,545 crore, with hospital revenue up 19% to INR 2,187 crore and diagnostics gross revenue up 10.2% to INR 407 crore. Consolidated operating EBITDA pre-ESOP rose 15.8% to INR 568 crore, but margin eased to 22.3% from 22.6%, with hospitals at 21.5% versus 22.1%. Management said the margin dip reflects new ramp-up units, higher legal costs, higher doubtful-debt provisions and the new ESOP charge, and it maintained the FY28 target of about 25% margin, now framed as post-ESOP. Net debt rose to INR 2,233 crore (1.01x EBITDA) from INR 1,869 crore a year earlier.

financial_highlights.change: +15.8% YoY; margin vs 22.6% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax before exceptional items

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1,869 crore and 0.92x at 30 June 2025

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,187 crore (+19%) and operating EBITDA INR 471 crore at 21.5% margin versus 22.1%. Like-for-like margin excluding new Punjab, Bengaluru and Delhi NCR leased facilities was about 22%. Renal sciences grew 28%, neurosciences 27% and orthopaedics 23%.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: Gross revenue INR 407 crore (+10.2%) and operating EBITDA INR 97 crore at 23.9% margin versus 23.0%. B2C:B2B mix improved to 53:47 from 51:49; preventive share rose to 14% from 12% and specialised to 35% from 34%. About 10.5 million tests processed and over 200 customer touch points added in the quarter.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 174 crore, up 13.3% YoY, about 8% of consolidated revenue, broadly in line with Q1 FY26.

guidance_outlook: Hospital EBITDA margin target of about 25% in roughly two years (FY28); management said it is now aspired to be achieved after ESOP cost, and Q1 is a dip versus this path.
Management retained the consolidated margin guidance; analysts had cited 150-200 bps hospital margin expansion for FY27, which management did not restate as ESOP-inclusive.
ESOP charge expected around INR 40 crore per quarter for the rest of FY27 if headcount is unchanged, falling to about INR 30 crore per quarter and then about INR 25 crore per quarter in year three.
Diagnostics revenue growth of about 12-13% and EBITDA margin of 24-25% for the remainder of the year, per the CFO; the Agilus CEO reiterated double-digit revenue growth guidance.
Plan to add about 400 beds in the remaining three quarters of FY27, including about 200 beds at FMRI pending an occupancy certificate expected imminently. Q1 added about 100 beds.

Manesar radiation oncology equipment expected to be commissioned by November 2026, after which it becomes a comprehensive oncology centre; Manesar and Greater Noida expected to reach mid-teens EBITDA margin by year-end or higher.
Capex: growth is expected to consume about 50% of EBITDA through brownfield expansion, excluding acquisitions; proton therapy in Gurgaon estimated at about INR 252 crore.
capex_capacity: Q1 added about 100 operational beds through brownfield expansion at Noida, Amritsar and Jalandhar; Manesar has about 187 beds operational at about 60% occupancy.

Robotics: Da Vinci Xi soft-tissue robots installed at Faridabad and Fortis Escorts Heart Institute Okhla; ortho robots installed at Jalandhar and Faridabad. Board approved a proton facility at the Gurgaon flagship, capex about INR 252 crore, still being finalised.
Entered Odisha via an O&M agreement for a 300-bed greenfield hospital in Cuttack; no capital committed.
Oncology build-out: three units (Faridabad brownfield block, Amritsar and Jaipur) are starting work to become full cancer hospitals.
Company is pursuing inorganic deals in existing clusters (Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Punjab, MMR, Kolkata); no details disclosed. Gleneagles O&M discussions with IHH ongoing.
demand_pricing: Hospital occupancy flat at 69% as occupied beds grew 17%; management said the core base consistently runs around 70% and levers can add 2-3 percentage points.

Oncology growth slowed from about 23-24% to about 5% because a 30% discount on chemo drug MRP under ECHS/CGHS pricing is hitting Punjab, Jaipur and NCR units; management expects 10-12% growth going forward.
Doctor poaching described as ongoing but not a major concern; ESOP scheme is broad-based across zones, covering roughly 55-60% doctors and administrative staff.
Diagnostics market described as competitive; management acknowledged muted or stagnant growth in prior periods due to rebranding, and the Agilus CEO (recently joined) is reworking plans.
Gleneagles O&M fee is 3% of revenue, about INR 6 crore booked in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP charge for FY27 and the next two years, and can consolidated margin improve by 100 bps in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the charge will be higher initially and fall over about three years; it still maintained margin guidance, citing cost savings and efficiency gains from the ESOP.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% margin target pre- or post-ESOP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 25% target now aspires to be achieved after ESOP cost, expected in about two years, with levers including ramp-up of new units (from -0.4% drag to +1%), new doctor teams, lower legal costs and recovery of doubtful debt provisions.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Manesar and Greater Noida margins below 10%, and when will they reach 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar had 187 beds operational at about 60% occupancy with radiation oncology due by November; management expects both hospitals to be in the mid-teens EBITDA margin by year-end or higher.

qa_highlights.question: Diagnostics growth lags industry; what are the challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: The Agilus CEO, in role about 10 days, said the company is reworking plans; B2C mix target rises to 55% and then 58%, and the company cited a rebrand and lab-network rationalisation affecting growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the oncology slowdown and is it chemo-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the chemo pricing mechanism with a 30% MRP discount for ECHS and CGHS beneficiaries is the cause; oncology growth fell to about 5% from 23-24%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex guidance and are acquisitions expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth capex is about 50% of EBITDA excluding acquisitions for the 2,000-bed expansion; inorganic deals are being pursued, expected to be in focus clusters, with no details yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are diagnostics margin and growth expectations for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO guided diagnostics revenue growth of about 12-13% and EBITDA margin of 24-25% for the remainder of the year.

risks_watch: Hospital margin dilution: Q1 at 21.5% versus 22.1%, with new units still dragging, ESOP charge of about INR 40 crore per quarter and rising doubtful-debt provisions from government and TPA payors.
Oncology pricing pressure from the chemo drug pricing mechanism in ECHS/CGHS segments; growth fell to about 5%.
Diagnostics growth lagging peers (about 10% vs industry about 15%) amid leadership change and reworking of plans.
Legal costs linked to the Delhi High Court proceedings (Gleneagles-related, per call context) continue into coming quarters.
Net debt up to INR 2,233 crore with capex plus inorganic spend; watch leverage versus 1.01x.
Manesar occupancy and oncology commissioning by November; Gleneagles O&M and IHH discussions outcome.

Diagnostics commentary was more defensive, with the new CEO still reworking plans.
key_quotes: We are pretty confident that we are still on track.
Overall, in two years' time, we are quite hopeful that we will be reaching to 25%.
We are aspiring to achieve 25% EBITDA margin after running the ESOP cost.
We are completely on the path that we will be able to achieve similar levels within, say, next few quarters.

rows.why: Net debt rose to INR 2,233 crore (1.01x EBITDA) from INR 1,869 crore (0.92x) a year earlier, with growth capex at ~50% of EBITDA plus pursued acquisitions.

532851|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR2,140 crores while PAT slipped to INR139 crores on a INR9 crore deferred tax charge; Q4 grew about 19%.
532851|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of resilience, with full-year revenue up about 7% to INR2,140 crores, gross profit up about 5% to INR675 crores, and EBITDA up about 3% to INR227 crores. PAT fell slightly from INR142 crores to INR139 crores, which management attributed to a roughly INR9 crore increase in deferred tax. Q4 revenue grew about 19%, with premium products up about 24%, but May was sluggish and the company is waiting for monsoon rains. Management guided to positive top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27, with the first quarter as the first visible test, while raw material inflation of nearly 10% or more supports pricing.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR142 crores; deferred tax up ~INR9 crores
supported by B2C and B2B; premium products ~24%
per CFO; management also cited FY growth above 7%

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Contributed 73% of FY26 sales. Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are 60-63% of B2C; management targets 60-70% in four years.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Contributed 22% of FY26 sales. Management says B2B held last year's level in April and expects growth in May and the rest of the year.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Contributed 5% of FY26 sales. Management targets 10% in 2-3 years, with CDMO and technical exports as drivers; CDMO work is at trial stage.

segments.name: Product categories (FY26 vs FY25)
segments.commentary: Patented products INR322 crores (vs ~INR330 crores); combination products INR324 crores (vs INR311 crores); in-licensed INR226 crores (vs INR229 crores); 5 products launched in FY26 INR40 crores; FY25 launches rose from INR23 crores to INR82 crores.

segments.name: Herbicides
segments.commentary: Contributed 39% of last year's sales. Price decline from off-patent competition hit last year; management expects quantities and a good increase this year as prices stabilise.

segments.name: Kaeros (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR110-111 crores; PAT above INR5 crores in its second year after acquisition for under INR6 crores. Management expects revenue to at least double in FY27 and contribute 5-8% of IIL volume.

guidance_outlook: Management expects both top line and bottom line to be positive in FY27, with results visible from Q1; management said the number is flat so far and depends on June monsoon.

Management believes the company is well placed to benefit from raw material inflation of up to about 10% or more, since its inventory of close to INR800 crores was bought before the price rise; management expects a small margin increase, with the size dependent on demand.
Management said EBITDA margins have already crossed double digits and it wishes to improve them further, without giving a number.
Working capital cycle target: management called a reduction from 140-150 days to 120 days achievable, with the timing dependent on the season.
Finance cost target: management internally targets a reduction of at least 25-30% in FY27.
Capex for FY27 is largely maintenance, in the range of INR25-30 crores after current projects are completed.
capex_capacity: Dahej: a new building (L&T) has begun manufacturing; management expects it to break even and be profitable by Diwali.
Technical plants at all sites have reached breakeven.
Sotanala: formulation start targeted around Diwali; whether it is billed depends on a CFO investment decision.
Sotanala technical plant: first of two buildings targeted for March-April 2027 for early kharif start; second building to follow based on market yield.
Management says Sotanala and Dahej provide sufficient capacity headroom for growth. About INR94 crores was invested in new products from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Industry: geopolitical tension has created supply constraints; raw material prices rose by nearly 10% and more for crude-linked products, shifting the market to a supplier-driven environment.
Two price increases were taken in April; the first was well received, but the second needed discounts in May. A June price increase is under consideration.
May was sluggish due to heat, and farmers are waiting for monsoon rains; El Nino and crop-mix changes in dry crops are key risks.
Herbicides are gaining traction as manual labour costs rise, but specialty herbicides from competitors are lowering prices.
Management says it sets no write-offs; unsold stock is taken back from the channel at season end and reformulated or moved between regions.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company benefit from its approximately INR800 crore inventory as raw material prices rise, given smaller competitors may lack stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed, saying the company plans from Diwali to Holi and bought stock before the price rise; the benefit depends on converting that stock into sales as the kharif season starts in June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of volume and value growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volume grew 5% and value 14%; FY26 volume grew 5% and value 2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 target for the working capital cycle and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle target is 120 days from 140-150 days, which management called achievable. Management internally targets a 25-30% cut in finance cost; the FY26 consolidated finance cost was INR16.87 crores against INR6.86 crores in FY25, driven by higher inventory, bank limit use and INR94 crores of new-product investment.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kaeros positioned against the Tractor/IIL brand and the partner products?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaeros will run a parallel distribution network with its own brand and a sales-only team. It is positioned as a follower to IIL, which gets first access to partnership products from Corteva, Nissan and OAT. Kaeros is not positioned as a cheaper brand; it will sell at a 2-3% initial discount.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of premium products and can it reach 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are 60-63% of B2C. Management targets 60-70% in four years, so 70% will take three to four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D success rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said success rates vary: about 9,000-10,000 molecules screened a year, with a dozen trial teams testing 500-600 products to yield roughly 10-15 launches. Reverse engineering has higher success rates. The first Indian patent filing is pending IUPAC name approval.

risks_watch: Working capital remains elevated: inventory was higher and DSO is being worked on to reduce it; cash conversion is a stated priority.
Finance cost rose sharply from INR6.86 crores to INR16.87 crores (consolidated); a reduction of 25-30% is the internal target.
Monsoon and El Nino conditions; May was sluggish, and June price increase is not yet decided.
Second April price increase needed discounts in May, showing channel resistance to pricing.

532853|2026-03.headline: Asahi Songwon Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 30.2% YoY to Rs 23 crore, with margin at 15.6% on price pass-through in Blue pigments.
532853|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 144 crore, up 19.4% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 23 crore (15.6% margin vs 8.58% in Q3 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25) and PAT of Rs 10.82 crore. For FY26, revenue fell 4.78% to Rs 535.48 crore while PAT rose 5.48% to Rs 17.78 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to raw-material price pass-through and operational efficiencies in Blue pigments, with a small inventory gain, and said the API price decline of the prior three years has reversed. Gokul Jaykrishna handed day-to-day CEO duties to his son Arjun Jaykrishna, while remaining Managing Director.

segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive and cash break-even reached. FY26 revenue Rs 78 crore with PBT loss of Rs 2.42 crore; management expects PBT break-even in FY27. Capacity is 2,400 tpa, utilisation about 65% per management, with a planned Rs 10-15 crore brownfield expansion to about 1.5x once utilisation reaches 75-85%.

segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive. Volumes grew about 18% CAGR over three years, but realisations fell 40-45% since acquisition; Pregabalin prices are about 15% above the bottom. Pregabalin is 60-70% of API business. Chattral intermediates run at about 60-70% and finished APIs at about 30%. Q4 API revenue was reported as about Rs 30 crore with EBIT of about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA across all three segments to at least maintain Q4 FY26 margins, with an aim to improve.

Long-term margin targets: about 13% EBITDA for AZO and 15-16% for API; Mitesh Patel said Chattral and Atlas could reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex, at 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years.

Management aims for Rs 1,000 crore group revenue within the next few years, with priority on sustaining revenue first.

Peak debt was Rs 220 crore after the completed four-year capex cycle; debt is falling faster than internal estimates.
demand_pricing: Blue pricing is set quarterly with MNC customers; Q4 benefit was partly locked in, so further benefit expected in Q1 and Q2. Mitesh Patel put the price increase at about 20%, and management said prices across pigments and crude rose meaningfully on raw-material tightness.
Management said China raised prices about 30-40% due to lower export incentives and VAT rebates, roughly doubled ocean freight and higher crude-linked raw material costs.

US tariffs hit AZO and Blue exports, including via India-made value-added products; US business has revived since tariffs eased but has not returned to normal. AZO export customers have restarted testing.
Management said Europe remains in a structural slowdown; India remains the main AZO growth market.
Management says the cyclical slowdown appears to be bottoming, and no new pigment capacity is expected in the industry.

qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jaykrishna said the strategy was to pass through as much raw-material inflation as possible via long-term supplier and customer relationships. He did not quantify the split and said revenue was under pressure while the bottom line held.

qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said margins reflect internal strategy, some inventory addition, and operating efficiencies. Gokul Jaykrishna later put the inventory gain as marginal, since the company held finished goods bought before the war.

qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said a one-time receipt of renewable-energy billing rebate, pending for two years, drove the drop. Management expects power and fuel as a percentage of sales to be lower than before but not at Q4 levels every quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Mitesh Patel said the two facilities can reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex and 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years. Arjun said API EBITDA depends on pricing, and management said the subsidiaries could reach about Rs 50 crore EBITDA at peak.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 57 stores opened and 1 closed in Q1 (381 at June 30, 2026), crossed 400 after quarter-end, with 170-200 openings guided for FY27 and 15-20 sites finalised monthly; MOU signed for next 100 stores.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue guided to grow at least 50% in FY27 with 170-200 openings on top of 381 stores; Q1 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore and SSSG was ~7.5%, though management said past price hikes reduced volume slightly.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation metric was disclosed and no new plant or capex programme is discussed; growth is store-led and funded from internal accruals, creditor-day release of INR150-200 crore and bank limits, with no QIP planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held all FY27 guidance (at least 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, 29-30% gross margin) despite Q1 SSSG at ~7.5% and gross margin below range, and July-August trends were called too early to judge.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 SSSG was ~7.5% against an 8-10% full-year target, gross margin of 28.6% sits below the 29-30% guided range, and full-price sales fell to ~90% from 92%, with the recovery depending on festive sell-through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or category launch was discussed; kids' wear is ~25% of sales but no new line was flagged.

rows.label: 4-5% garment MRP increase from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Raw material inflation hits from Q3 as H1 orders were placed earlier, and management plans to pass a 4-5% rise in garment cost to consumers, saying past hikes cut volume slightly but were offset by ASP.

rows.label: Creditor-day normalisation releases INR150-200 crore
rows.why: Creditor days are ~45-50 against a 45-50 target after vendor prepayments inflated working capital, and inventory of ~100 days is to be cut later; cash release depends on this normalising.

rows.label: RK Retail acquisition consolidates from Q2 FY27
rows.why: The brief says RK Retail acquisition will consolidate from Q2, which adds to revenue, but no size or contribution figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on store expansion, the 50% growth guide and funding without a QIP, but cautious and deflective on July-August demand, gross margin recovery and new-store productivity; analysts pushed on gross margin and the new-store productivity gap.

532868|2026-03.headline: DLF posted a record FY26 collection of over INR 13,500 crore (+15% YoY) and zero gross debt in development, with FY26 sales bookings of INR 20,143 crore in line with guidance.
532868|2026-03.overview: Management reported a strong close to FY26, citing record collections of over INR 13,500 crore (+15%) and cash surplus of over INR 7,700 crore (+25%). FY26 sales bookings were INR 20,143 crore, in line with guidance despite deferral of a couple of launches, with Q4 sales of about INR 3,967 crore led by Dahlias. Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR 2,452 crore with reported net profit of INR 1,256 crore; FY26 net profit was INR 4,256 crore (+16%). The rental business shows a 95% occupancy portfolio of 50 million sq ft and a 4-5 year NOI growth guidance of mid-teens, with 20-25% CAGR on a longer basis. Management steered the Q&A away from presales volume toward margins and cash flows.

financial_highlights.value: INR 14,155 crore, of which ~INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts

financial_highlights.metric: DCCDL FY26 revenue / EBITDA / PBT before exceptional
financial_highlights.value: ~INR 7,400 crore / over INR 5,700 crore / INR 2,726 crore

segments.name: Rental (annuity) business
segments.commentary: Rental portfolio of 50 million sq ft at 95% occupancy; FY26 NOI growth of about 34-35% driven by assets completed late FY25 reaching full lease. Non-SEZ office occupancy 98-99%, SEZ 88-89%, and income loss from vacancy down to ~3.5%.

segments.name: Development (DevCo)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales of INR 20,143 crore; Dahlias sales about INR 5,000 crore in FY26, guided to INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27. Management targets ~INR 9,000-10,000 crore of margin creation and INR 7,000-8,000 crore of DevCo FCF annually.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Existing mall income expected to grow 10-11% in FY27, plus three new malls. Midtown Plaza 95% leased and operational; Summit Plaza 95-97% leased, opening likely second half of July; Promenade Goa 50% leasing line of sight, completion around August.

segments.name: Office (Atrium Place, Downtown)
segments.commentary: Atrium Place (JV with Hines, 3.2 million sq ft) fully leased; three towers have OC and fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27, generating ~INR 700 crore rent. Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft ~500,000 sq ft leased, completion expected Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales guidance of ~INR 20,000 crore maintained; management said upside possible if demand stays strong.
Annual margin creation of ~INR 9,000 crore guided to continue.
Rental NOI guidance: mid-teens growth in NOI and 20-25% CAGR over the next 4-5 years, though management cautioned FY26's 34-35% growth should not be extrapolated.
FY27 exit rental of ~INR 8,200 crore across DCCDL and the rest of DLF assets combined.
Launch pipeline of almost INR 20,000 crore for FY27, including a large DLF City launch (INR 8,000-9,000 crore or higher), Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa.
Dividend: no formal guidance given; ~two-thirds of dividend is funded by Cyber City's dividend to DLF.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 (Towers 5-8) completion late FY28/early FY29; Taramani completion Q2 FY28.

Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft: completion expected Q2 FY28; central atrium design change made.

Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2: 7.5 million sq ft integrated development (2 million sq ft mall, 5.5 million sq ft offices); Tower 7 (2.2 million sq ft) nearly fully leased; Towers 5 and 6 being leased; finishing late FY28/early FY29; iconic tower construction to start in ~2.5 years.
Westpark Mumbai pipeline above 5 million sq ft; ~900,000 sq ft launched so far, next phase of ~800,000 sq ft in FY27, then 500,000-600,000 sq ft.
SEZ portfolio of 16-17 million sq ft; ~4 million sq ft converted to non-processing areas. Chennai operating portfolio above 10 million sq ft, rising to 14-15 million sq ft.
demand_pricing: Dahlias (super luxury, Gurugram): 32 apartments sold in Q4 plus 2 Camellias; per-unit prices now ~INR 90-110 crore for the first phase units vs ~INR 60-75 crore at launch. Dahlias per sq ft pricing is about INR 1 lakh on super area vs Camellias ~INR 1.2 lakh (INR 80-150 crore per unit).
Office SEZ rentals: gap to Cyber City rentals narrowed to 10-12% for new take-up; Cyber City vacancy lowest in SEZ portfolio; Hyderabad SEZ vacancy 17-20%.
Chennai Taramani top-floor leases at INR 145-150 per sq ft; average realisation expected INR 125-130 per sq ft.

Management flagged that large tenants are reviewing internal processes, which could defer leasing decisions, though no portfolio impact so far; cited AI and Iran-US war as factors but said there was no impact yet.
Management declined to chase presales volume, saying margins and cash flows are the priority; said presales of INR 50,000 crore a year are possible given land bank.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the medium-term launch pipeline shown as ~INR 60,000 crore versus INR 67,000 crore earlier, and is the company less confident about the market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is a status update on a INR 1,14,000 crore 5-year launch pipeline announced ~2 years ago; launches are paced to market absorption and execution capacity, with further phases identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 launch and presales plan given the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pipeline is ~INR 20,000 crore, including a DLF City launch of INR 8,000-9,000 crore or more, Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa (approvals in place but a PIL pending).

qa_highlights.question: Why is presales growth limited to ~INR 20,000 crore versus peers at INR 30,000-35,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said presales is not the right metric and the company is chasing margins and cash flows; it could do INR 50,000 crore a year if chosen, with delivery capability the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 presales is expected from Dahlias and how much from the launch pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahlias sales were about INR 5,000 crore in FY26 and are expected at INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27; management expects INR 13,000-14,000 crore to come from the ~INR 20,000 crore launch pipeline, as not all launches will sell out at launch.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts and the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Badal Bagri said the RERA cash unlocks from FY27-28; uses are shareholder returns, DLF rental capex (committed), and opportunistic margin-accretive land deals. Revenue recognition is on completed-contract method, with large projects like Arbour delivering from FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend sustainable and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said about two-thirds of the dividend comes from Cyber City's dividend to DLF, and no dividend guidance is being offered, though the trajectory has been of continuing growth.

risks_watch: Rental NOI growth of 34-35% in FY26 was driven by one-time lease-up of assets completed late FY25; management cautioned against extrapolation.

Launch pipeline timing: Goa approvals subject to a PIL; Moti Nagar Phase 2 unlikely in FY27 and possibly FY28.
Dahlias sell-out and per-sq ft price trajectory is a key driver of FY27 presales; management admitted Dahlias pricing has moved fast.
Rising brokerage and overhead costs in Q4 linked to collections and year-end provisioning; management said full-year overheads should stay around current levels.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Taramani completion timelines, plus Atrium Place fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27.

532868|2026-06.headline: DLF Q1 FY27 net profit rose to INR 794 crore (from INR 766 crore) while pre-sales were muted at INR 657 crore amid Aureva launch deferment.
532868|2026-06.overview: DLF reported a resilient Q1 FY27 with collections of INR 2,406 crore, operating cash flow above INR 1,300 crore and net cash of INR 15,200 crore, of which close to INR 11,000 crore sits in RERA escrow accounts. Pre-sales were INR 657 crore, held back by the deferred Aureva senior living launch awaiting approvals and a deliberate pacing of Dahlias sales. Rental revenue was INR 1,605 crore with EBITDA of INR 476 crore, and occupancy stayed above 95% by space and 97% by value. DCCDL posted revenue up 10% YoY to INR 1,917 crore and PAT of INR 717 crore, up over 20%, though this included one-time tax entries. Management said FY28 would be the reporting inflection as large projects begin contributing under completed-contract accounting.

segments.name: Office rentals
segments.commentary: Vacancy is very low; newer assets Cyber Park, Atrium Place, Downtown Gurgaon and Downtown Chennai are nearly 100% leased. Rentals in the portfolio grew about 8.5%-9% from Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Midtown Plaza is fully operational, about 85% open and 96%-97% leased; Summit Plaza had a soft launch and is about 90% leased; Goa mall has OC, is 64% leased as of 31 July, and is targeted to open late 2026 or early 2027. Retail spend grew about 13.5%-14%.

segments.name: Residential (Dahlias, Golf Links)
segments.commentary: Dahlias is about 65% sold with 34 units sold in the quarter; price realisation is above INR 1 lakh per sq ft, reaching INR 1.20-1.25 lakh on higher floors, with entry ticket above INR 100 crore.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: DLF will act only as real estate developer and builder for data centres, not own technology or operate them; Data Center 3 in Noida expected to add rental around March-April 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY28 expected to be the reporting inflection point as large projects starting with Arbour contribute to P&L under completed-contract accounting.
Management hopes to stick to broad FY27 sales guidance; Goa residential shortfall would be about 10% of the INR 20,000 crore guidance and is expected to be covered.
Group exit rentals for FY27 guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.
Midtown Plaza and Summit Plaza expected to reach steady-state rentals by Q4 FY27; Goa to stabilise around May-June 2027; Atrium Place Tower 1 OC expected in September 2026.
Q2 and Q3 expected to be good quarters for office leasing as global companies and GCCs return to decision-making.
capex_capacity: Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Downtown Chennai Phase 2 construction at full speed; Gurgaon leasing about 40%, Taramani pre-leasing about 17%-18%.
Downtown Chennai Towers 4 and 5 (3.5 million sq ft) to complete by beginning of 2028; Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 by end 2029.
Atrium Place Tower 1 OC expected September 2026; all three new malls (Midtown, Summit, Goa) now operational in FY27 per management.
Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres consolidated) still on drawing board; sizing and launch decision expected within next year.
Land spend of about INR 545 crore over the last two quarters, including an INR 80 crore EMD for an NCR auction not yet concluded.
Mumbai project with potential above 5 million sq ft; launch targeted within FY27 or calendar 2026.
demand_pricing: Office demand slowed by AI-related hiring uncertainty and the Iran-US conflict since February; management sees GCC and large multinational enquiries returning in the last 4-5 weeks.

Gurgaon rentals: Atrium Place about INR 175 per sq ft weighted average, Downtown 4 about INR 150-155, Phase 2 leasing averaging INR 200; Cyber City existing rentals INR 140-150 versus INR 210-220 for newer buildings.

CAM costs rose about 2%-2.5% due to minimum wage revisions; no tenant pushback reported because CAM is audited annually and passed through.
Pre-sales pacing for Dahlias to be held until Experience Centre opens after Diwali; next Privana phase expected early 2027 as a high-rise scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Is the slowdown in Dahlias sustenance sales (34 units vs typical 12-15 units per quarter) deliberate?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pace was consciously managed around the Experience Centre opening after Diwali; Dahlias is about 65% sold and entry ticket is now above INR 100 crore, with some additional sales held back pending paperwork.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Goa residential launch slip without hurting the INR 20,000 crore sales guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said Goa accounted for only a couple of thousand crore, about 10% of guidance, and that the gap should be covered comfortably; all Goa approvals are in hand but the PIL is being addressed before taking customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the stabilised run-rate of group rental income and what ramp-up remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Midtown and Summit Plaza reach steady state by Q4 FY27, Goa by May-June 2027, and Atrium Place Tower 1 adds a full tower after its September OC; exit FY27 group rentals guided at INR 7,300-7,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will Cyber City 2 and the next commercial pipeline start?
qa_highlights.answer: Sriram Khattar said Cyber City 2 (70-80 acres) sizing and launch remain undecided with a decision expected within the next year; construction in Hyderabad or Cyber City is planned for sometime next year.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about Dahlias sales velocity versus price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said about 3.5 years of sales were achieved in 15-16 months, with roughly 3 years remaining; Ashok Tyagi said there is no direct binary between velocity and price, and the next phase depends on physical and commercial progress, implying a 3-year cycle.

532868|2026-09.headline: DLF Q2 FY27 booked INR 3,800 crore sales and reported INR 2,298 crore revenue, aided by a one-time INR 738 crore fair-value gain in other income.
532868|2026-09.overview: DLF reported new sales bookings of about INR 3,800 crore and collections of INR 2,780 crore, with operating cash flow of about INR 1,858 crore and net cash of about INR 15,100 crore after roughly INR 1,980 crore of dividend payout. Consolidated revenue of INR 2,298 crore included a one-time INR 738 crore valuation gain on a JV investment booked as other income, with EBITDA of INR 1,060 crore and net profit above INR 1,300 crore. Management said accounting revenue remains back-ended under completed-contract accounting until the pre-Arbour projects complete in FY28. Management flagged likely Q3 construction outflow slowdown from labour migration and Delhi GRAP restrictions.

532884|2026-06.headline: Refex Q1 FY27 standalone continuing revenue rose 76% YoY to INR619 crore, with EBITDA of INR105 crore (17% margin) and PAT of INR73.6 crore (+123%).
532884|2026-06.overview: Standalone continuing-operations revenue grew 76% YoY to INR619 crore and EBITDA rose to INR105 crore at a 17% margin, while PAT reached INR73.6 crore (11.9% margin). Ash and coal handling remained the largest contributor despite acute diesel shortages and logistics disruptions linked to geopolitical developments. Wind turbine execution started contributing INR295 crore in the quarter at near-zero margin, and the mobility demerger is progressing toward a shareholder meeting next month.

Q2 expected to be slower, Q3-Q4 to scale up. Management guides EBITDA margin of 15-18% and net margin of 10-12%.

segments.commentary: Asset-light premium corporate mobility; being demerged into a separate listed company. NCLT has approved convening shareholder and creditor meetings, with equity shareholder meeting scheduled for next month. Expected to exit discontinued operations by end of Q3 FY27.

segments.commentary: Fully discontinued as of the last quarter; part of discontinued operations.

532885|2026-03.headline: Central Bank of India Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR724 crore on a one-time INR632 crore DTA charge; FY26 net profit rose 15.43% to INR4,369 crore.
532885|2026-03.overview: FY26 business grew 15.60% to INR812,439 crore, with gross advances up 18.76% to INR344,516 crore and deposits up 13.38% to INR467,923 crore. Q4 net profit fell to INR724 crore from INR1,034 crore a year earlier, mainly due to a one-time INR632 crore hit from recognising deferred tax assets at 25% instead of 35%. Q4 operating profit rose 4.64% YoY to INR2,096 crore, but fell QoQ as treasury income (INR9 crore vs more than INR300 crore) and recoveries from written-off accounts (INR352 crore vs INR1,062 crore) dropped. Asset quality improved on a full-year basis: gross NPA 2.67% (down 51 bps YoY), net NPA 0.49%, slippage ratio 1.16% vs 1.45%.

marginal decline; Q4 about 2.9% excluding INR431 crore tax refund interest

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower treasury income (INR9 crore vs more than INR300 crore in Q3) and lower written-off recoveries (INR352 crore vs INR1,062 crore). Net profit was hit by the INR632 crore DTA charge. No stress signals have appeared so far from the Middle East situation.

qa_highlights.answer: Mukul Dandige attributed part of the rise to MSME accounts flagged in branch audits where credit submissions did not match business projections, and to some agriculture accounts. Government-scheme (MUDRA, PMEGP) accounts up to INR10 lakh also slipped; the normal run-rate is about INR800 crore a quarter.

Ongoing ECL-related provisions are estimated at INR600 crore to INR650 crore a year, offset by a tax benefit of roughly INR600 crore to INR800 crore. The full simulation is not complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM rise about 30 bps QoQ when yields and funding costs were flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Dandige said a INR431 crore income-tax interest refund booked in Q4 added to NIM. Excluding it, NIM was about 2.89% to 2.9% in Q4 vs 2.96% in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are standard asset provisions and gold loan details?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard asset provisions are about 0.7% to 0.8% of standard assets, around INR2,800 crore to INR2,900 crore in total, including the INR1,525 crore ECL provision and RBI restructuring provisions. Gold loans are about INR28,000 crore, growing 8.6%.

532885|2026-06.headline: Central Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, with advances up 28.58% YoY and gross NPA at 2.60%.
532885|2026-06.overview: Central Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 global business of ₹833,320 crore (up 18.29% YoY), with deposits up 11.68% to ₹478,972 crore and gross advances up 28.58% to ₹354,348 crore. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.60% (down 53 bps YoY), net NPA at 0.49%, and slippage ratio at 0.29%. Management said the quarter's advances growth was driven partly by a low base in corporate loans, and quarter-on-quarter advances growth was only about 2.85%. Liquidity coverage ratio fell sharply from 235% to 156%, as the bank deployed liquidity into loans.

532891|2026-03.headline: Puravankara Q4 FY26 presales rose 190% YoY to INR3,547 crore; FY27 presales guidance set at INR11,200 crore and debt reduction target of INR750 crore.
532891|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter on sales and handovers, with presales of INR3,547 crore (up 190% YoY and 151% QoQ) and total income of INR1,541 crore (up 173% YoY) driven by 1,301 handovers. FY26 presales hit a record INR7,407 crore (up 55%) and collections a record INR4,258 crore (up 15%). Net debt was INR2,321 crore at March 31, 2026, down INR160 crore in the quarter, and cost of debt fell to 11.05%. Management guided FY27 presales of INR11,200 crore and a gross debt reduction of about INR750 crore, excluding new borrowing for business development. Collections, interest cost and FY27 delivery guidance drew the most pointed questions and several were deferred to offline follow-up.

segments.name: Residential sales
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales volume was 3.01 million sq ft (vs 1.42 million sq ft in Q4 FY25) at average realisation of INR11,787 per sq ft (up 37% YoY). FY26 volume was 7.25 million sq ft at INR10,213 per sq ft (up 21%).

segments.name: Handovers
segments.commentary: Handed over 1,301 homes (1.67 million sq ft) in Q4 FY26 and 3,747 homes (4.25 million sq ft) in FY26.

segments.name: Launches
segments.commentary: Launched three new projects (Purva SilverSky, Purva Northern Lights, Purva Estrella) and seven new phases in FY26, totalling 6.39 million sq ft. Northern Lights realisation is about INR10,700 per sq ft and it contributed INR1,100-1,200 crore to Q4 presales. Lokhandwala contributed slightly over INR800 crore in Q4.

segments.name: Commercial assets
segments.commentary: Aerocity has received OC and leasing has started; Zentech OC is expected within the month and is about 40-45% leased or sold. FY26 commercial sales and leasing was about 2.6 lakh sq ft.

segments.name: Starworth
segments.commentary: Not a reporting segment; order book is above INR2,000 crore and FY25 financials are on the website, with FY26 to follow.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales target of about INR11,200 crore, of which about 48% from sustained sales and 52% from new launches; about INR7,000 crore expected from the South and the rest from West and Commercial.
Gross debt reduction target of about INR750 crore for FY27, excluding incremental borrowing for business development; scheduled repayment is INR836 crore this year.

Collections expected to grow in double digits in FY27; management suggested 45-50% of the INR7,400 crore sales from the big launches could be collected in the first year (exact figure to be shared offline).
Estimated surplus cash flow of INR19,290 crore: INR8,816 crore from ongoing projects, INR2,131 crore from exiting commercial assets, and INR8,343 crore from the launch pipeline.
Launch pipeline of 14.85 million sq ft with GDV of INR22,547 crore; Bandra launch expected between Dussehra and Diwali after members vacate by end-June.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 56.48 million sq ft, of which about 21 million sq ft is earmarked for the launch guidance, leaving about 35 million sq ft.

FY26 business development added over 12 million sq ft and about INR15,200 crore GDV across six projects, including Chembur (INR2,100 crore GDV), Malabar Hills (INR2,700 crore), Hennur Road JD (INR1,300 crore), Baglagere JD (INR1,000 crore), Attibele 53.5 acres (INR4,800 crore) and Northern Bengaluru JD (INR3,300 crore).
Malabar Hills: development agreement complete, registration in about 45 days, approvals expected in 9-12 months, pricing INR115,000-120,000 per sq ft on carpet area.
Two under-construction assets delivered, totalling about 2 million sq ft; FY27 residential delivery guidance to be shared offline.
Commercial: planning new verticals including data centres, warehousing and retail (about 3 lakh sq ft retail in Thane), with NCR (Delhi, Noida, Gurugram) as the expansion focus; no timelines given.
demand_pricing: Management says the Bengaluru market is steady rather than frenzied, with about 30% of the last launch sold; AI and GCC demand is seen as supportive.
NRI demand held up after the strong launch quarter; management says rupee depreciation may attract outside money but is watching global uncertainty.
Construction costs are rising about 6-7% due to diesel prices; management says margins and contingencies absorb this for now.
Project margins: new launches target above 20% gross margin (Northern Lights about 20-21%, Purva Estrella slightly above 20%); plotted development 30-40% gross margin.
Housing sales in top 8 cities were about 84,800 units, with homes above INR10 million at about 53% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Launch timing and confidence in the launch pipeline, including Bandra?
qa_highlights.answer: Bandra launch targeted between Dussehra and Diwali, with a GDV of about INR2,700 crore for the saleable portion. Management says most of the pipeline (INR22,547 crore) should launch despite past delays from Bengaluru approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Collection outlook for FY27 given weak YoY growth and flat Western collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections will grow in double digits, with about 45-50% of the FY26 sales expected to be collected in the first year; the exact figure will be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense rise to about INR600-650 crore, and how does the NCD accounting work?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the increase reflects debt raised for business development, and that fair-value accounting for some instruments adds to P&L cost. Cost on that instrument is above 11.05%. Detailed working to follow offline.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR750 crore debt reduction apply to gross or net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it refers to gross debt, with scheduled repayment of INR836 crore this year; excess collections and project-level sweeps may add to that.

qa_highlights.question: Commercial leasing traction at Zentech and Aerocity?
qa_highlights.answer: Zentech is about 40-45% leased or sold before OC; Aerocity has many GCC RFPs of over 2 million sq ft and large deals are expected in the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Collections: FY26 collections grew only 15% against 55% presales growth, and the company has not given a collection number for FY27.
Interest cost of about INR600-650 crore on roughly INR3,900-4,000 crore gross debt; management is to provide reconciliation offline.
Launch execution risk in Bengaluru amid approval changes (e-Khata, Greater Bengaluru Authority) and the Bandra vacation timeline.
Cost inflation of 6-7% from diesel prices and geopolitical impact on the RBI's FY27 growth outlook (6.9%).
Delivery guidance for FY27 residential and the timing of Zentech OC and Aerocity leasing remain unquantified.

532891|2026-06.headline: Puravankara Q1 FY27 presales rose 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores and PAT turned positive at INR25 crores; FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crores reiterated.

Collections rose 40% to INR1,199 crores and 745 homes (0.94 million sq ft) were handed over. Total income rose 63% YoY to INR877 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 25% from 15%, and PAT was INR25 crores versus a loss of INR69 crores a year earlier. Management kept FY27 presales guidance and the INR700 crores debt-reduction target, while adding four Bengaluru land opportunities (GDV ~INR5,200 crores) and signing a sale of Purva Zentech to ICICI Prudential AMC at ~INR625 crores EV.

532898|2026-03.headline: POWERGRID delivered ₹28,206 crore capitalisation and ~₹40,000 crore capex in FY26, guiding FY27 capex to ₹37,000 crore and capitalisation to ₹30,000 crore.
532898|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 capex (close to ₹40,000 crore against an initial ₹28,000 crore guide) and capitalisation (₹28,206 crore against a ₹25,000 crore commitment) both beat guidance. Standalone PAT rose 4% to about ₹15,921 crore and consolidated PAT rose 3% to about ₹15,928 crore, with total income of ₹47,684 crore versus ₹47,459 crore. Management flagged a natural RTM revenue decline as assets reach 12 years, offset by FY26 capitalisation that it expects to flow into FY27 revenue. The pipeline was described as ₹1.7 lakh crore of works in hand and ₹1.1 lakh crore under bidding, with new avenues in BESS, integrated storage under Section 62, and the first international PPP in Kenya.

segments.commentary: Works in hand of about ₹28,000 crore. Revenue is on a natural downward trajectory after assets complete 12 years, offset in FY26 by ~₹1,700 crore of depreciation-related gaps covered by other income items.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,195 crore; first 400G interface in India, first international long-distance link to Bhutan, and a 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible in the next quarter.

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,755 crore versus ₹799 crore in FY25, with 39 domestic orders and 62 ongoing projects, and 8 international orders across 25 countries.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 capex expected above ₹40,000 crore, with management indicating a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range.

FY27 expected to show full revenue benefit of FY26 capitalisation, which came mainly in the later part of FY26.

Integrated storage (BESS) capacity target not yet given; management said numbers would follow once Section 62 regulatory clarity emerges.
Pang-Kaithal HVDC project excluded from the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand pending Government of India review.
capex_capacity: Capitalisation of 4,765 ckm of transmission lines and 72,055 MVA of substation capacity added in FY26; 9 new substations taking the total to 291, and total transmission lines at 1.84 lakh ckm and 624 GVA transformation capacity at 31 March 2026.

demand_pricing: Works in hand ₹1.7 lakh crore (TBCB ₹1.37 lakh crore, RTM ₹28,000 crore, others ₹4,200 crore), excluding Pang-Kaithal HVDC.

Under-bidding pipeline of ₹1.1 lakh crore, including ₹5,270 crore of intra-State; major projects include Barmer Phase 4, Vizag Green Hydrogen, Jam Khambhaliya, Krishnagiri, Lakadia, ERWR and Nawada-Durgapur.
Management cited a ₹7.9 lakh crore opportunity under the 900+ GW by 2036 anchor programme and ₹6.4 lakh crore from Brahmaputra basin hydro; 22 HVDC schemes (127 GW) are in planning or bidding.
Intra-State TBCB thresholds are ₹150-250 crore by state; the smallest project POWERGRID has bid was about ₹60 crore.
Management said electricity share in the energy basket is about 22% and is expected to rise, supporting transmission demand.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the Q4 FY26 EBITDA decline and whether new TBCB projects use service concession accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the natural RTM tariff dip after 12 years of asset life; new BOOT-method TBCB projects are accounted for using the financial lease model.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and commissioning expectations for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 expected beyond ₹40,000 crore, in a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range. Capitalisation guided at ₹30,000 crore for FY27 and about ₹35,000 crore for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block versus NCT cost variance on projects and inflation indicators?

qa_highlights.question: Market share and whether competitive intensity in TBCB is rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has bid TBCB for about 14 years and selects projects by risk-return framework rather than volume; it did not indicate a change in intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Equity IRR on TBCB projects given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns could be better than the 11-13% range, as cost-plus RTM rewards cost but TBCB rewards efficiency, and change-in-law provisions protect against surprises.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing of capex and capitalisation in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing depends on individual project completions, expects an even spread across quarters, and noted that the Q4-heavy FY26 was incidental.

qa_highlights.question: Regulated equity on standalone and consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulated equity exists only in standalone; TBCB projects have no regulated equity.

532898|2026-06.headline: POWERGRID Q1 FY27 PAT flat at Rs 3,598 crore (vs Rs 3,631 crore QoQ) as regulatory drag of ~Rs 560 crore offset Rs 790 crore transmission-charge growth.

Capitalisation of Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 was about 3.1x the prior-year Q1 figure of Rs 1,683 crore, against a FY27 guidance of Rs 30,000 crore. Receivable days fell to about 12 from 19.41, with Rs 11,404 crore realised against Rs 10,963 crore billed.

segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 252 crore; 16 domestic and 3 international orders, footprint in about 25 countries.

532899|2026-06.headline: Kaveri Seed Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 815 crore from Rs 945 crore (about -14%) on a weak El Nino monsoon, with EBITDA margin held near 35%.
532899|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 815 crore against Rs 945 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA at Rs 285 crore (vs Rs 332 crore) and net profit at Rs 271.3 crore (vs Rs 316 crore) as stated on the call. Management attributed the decline to a delayed, deficient monsoon that shortened the sowing window, cutting maize sales in Karnataka and weakening demand in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. Cotton was flat YoY at Rs 213.43 crore while non-cotton was Rs 601.57 crore, and new products gained share in cotton and maize. Management said the quarter's margin was helped by lower production cost (down 4-5%) and that inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY, prompting lower production next year.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Sales fell sharply (about 40% decline per analyst question, not disputed by management); Karnataka sowing was about one-fifth done by mid-June. New single-cross hybrids are over 20% of maize sales.

Product pipeline described as among the best in 10 years, with Madhya Pradesh hybrids newer and not yet at scale.

Cotton MRP is government-capped; management said Kaveri realises higher prices than many peers in the top three cotton segments.

Management said subsidiaries (sales of about 10-12 lakh cotton packets this year) operate as separate competitors, and that their revenue is booked independently.

Management reaffirmed a three-year guidance to double AUM, income and net profit, and said co-lending is excluded from that base.

532923|2026-06.headline: Renaissance Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT jumped 288% to INR26 crores, but management guided revenue down as low-return customers are exited.

Management said it will exit low-return customer businesses in the customer brands segment, which lowers revenue run-rate by INR400 crores by year-end, while it targets bottom-line growth above 30% for FY27.

532926|2026-03.headline: Jyothy Labs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.7% to INR717 crores, but EBITDA margin fell about 330 bps to 13.5% on crude-linked input inflation and lower realisations.
