qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 revenue slowdown due to supply chain or geopolitical issues?

qa_highlights.question: Is the $1 billion revenue target still valid, and how does it reconcile with 25% growth?

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build-up and debt: how will working capital and capex be funded?

qa_highlights.question: What is the HVDC timeline?

532928|2026-09.headline: TARIL Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 66% YoY to INR709 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 16.1%, with order book at INR7,237 crore (+32% YoY).
532928|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR709 crore (+66% YoY, +27% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR114 crore (+203% YoY), with margin at 16.1% versus 8.8% a year earlier, which management attributed to higher utilisation and operating leverage. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,268 crore (+35% YoY) and EBITDA INR185 crore (14.6% margin). Order inflow in Q2 was INR1,169 crore (+97% YoY off a low base), and the unexecuted order book stood at INR7,237 crore, executable over 18-24 months. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 25% growth and 9-10% PAT margin, while working-capital days (about 154) remain the key drag on cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation per MVA and capex on Changodar?
qa_highlights.answer: Average realisation about INR7 lakh per MVA; Changodar capex about INR150 crore for about 35,000 MVA capacity.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it maintains the INR3,200 crore FY27 revenue target and the 9-10% PAT margin. It needs to execute about INR900 crore per quarter.

532929|2026-03.headline: Brigade FY26 pre-sales fell 5% to INR 7,424 crore on approval delays; FY27 pre-sales guided to at least 20% growth, aiming for INR 9,000 crore.

segments.commentary: Revenue about 4x YoY on a low base, but Q1 contribution weak amid raw material cost increases, pricing pressure and shorter customer delivery timelines. Management expects improvement from Q2 but calls it a continuing concern.

guidance_outlook: Sales expected to rise sequentially each quarter; Q2 to date reportedly shows continued strong YoY growth.
EBITDA margin expected to improve gradually in Q2–Q3 as raw material price settlements with customers conclude by end-Q2/early Q3.
Target of about 12–13% sustainable margin for automotive ancillaries on OEM business (management view, versus about 19% cited by analyst as current).
Targeted to be net debt free within 3 years.
Aftermarket expected to keep growing around 30%; new distribution warehouse in West India planned this quarter.
Tooling output to increase 20% in FY27 versus 148 molds in FY26.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex focused on EPDM capability: one new line operational in Q2 FY27 and two further lines planned in FY27.
Tooling toolroom expansion and land acquisition in west area near Sambhaji Nagar planned in FY27.
Hutchinson-linked technology investment in machines and equipment for new product development (no JV; amount not given).
Industrial product business needs no major capex (low-value tooling made in-house).
Capacity utilisation at 73% in Q1; tooling at 84%.
demand_pricing: Industry posted record Q1 sales: passenger vehicles +25% YoY to 1.27 million units; two-wheelers +20.3%; commercial vehicles +18.3%; three-wheelers +29.7%; vehicle exports record Q1.
Raw material cost up about 4%; about 2% passed to customers so far, with the remaining about 50% of the increase still under negotiation.

Technology partnership with Hutchinson (sealing systems) signed; initial focus on glass run channel products for Indian market. Management expects clarity on revenue by end-2026; no revenue figure given. Named competitors: SFC, Anand Nishikawa, Toyota Bussei.
Mahindra: Tier 1 sealing products SOP scheduled for Q3 FY27; Tier 2 injection moulding tooling and sunroof sealing in development.
Management said pre-COVID margins are very difficult to regain given changed raw material prices and competitive pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from the Hutchinson partnership over the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical estimate; products are being co-developed for all customers with focus on India, and clarity on timing expected by end-2026. Focus product is glass run channel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating margin plan and when will margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4% raw material inflation with about 2% passed through; the rest expected to be settled by end-Q2 or early Q3. Internal margin targets exist but were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the JV exit proceeds be used?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR100 crores received; INR8 crores for tax; 25% of the remainder for working capital; the rest for strategic capex in EPDM, tooling expansion and western land.

qa_highlights.question: When does the battery business reach breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 contribution was weak; management hopes for improvement from Q2 but acknowledged it remains a concern without giving a breakeven figure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth momentum continue through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 to date shows strong growth and expects sequential sales increases; not a one-off from low base or deferred orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin level and why has top-line growth been muted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 12–13% sustainable margin for OEM ancillaries; attributed past slow growth to actions taken over 2–3 years and to electrical content gains not reaching the company's sealing and moulded parts portfolio.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: about 50% of the 4% cost increase still unrecovered from customers; settlement timing (end-Q2/early Q3) is a key watch item.
Battery segment losses continuing; Q1 contribution described as weak.
Industrial Products sales moderation in Q1; seasonality versus trend.
Geopolitical developments, commodity price volatility and global supply chain dynamics flagged by management.
Hutchinson partnership revenue remains unquantified; timing clarity only by end-2026.
Debt: net debt-free target within 3 years; finance cost trajectory not quantified.
Restructuring execution: tooling hive-off by Q3 FY27 and Avinya merger by Q4 FY27.
key_quotes: And quarter-on-quarter, I think what we are expecting is the sales numbers to increase.
For the balance 50% price increases, we are in the discussion with the customer.
So the pre-COVID prices is very difficult to achieve again, it is clear.
But we are hopeful that quarter 2 onwards, things may start get better, but it still remains a cause of concern for us.

It was cautious and vague on raw material pass-through, battery losses and margin timing, and gave no numbers on Hutchinson revenue or a battery breakeven point.

rows.why: One new EPDM line is operational in Q2 FY27 and two further lines are planned in FY27, with company capacity utilisation at only 73% in Q1 and tooling at 84%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says Q2 to date shows strong YoY growth and sales should rise sequentially each quarter, but no numeric revenue guidance was given.

rows.why: Mahindra Tier 1 sealing products SOP is scheduled for Q3 FY27, 345 aftermarket SKUs were launched (portfolio 1,312), and Hutchinson co-developed glass run channel products are expected to have timing clarity by end-2026 with no revenue figure given.

rows.why: Orders won in the quarter rose 51.8% YoY to INR131 crores, with EV about INR64 crores, which supports revenue growth in the coming quarters.

rows.when: Tooling by Q3 FY27; Avinya merger by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management has a dated restructuring plan, but battery Q1 contribution was weak after revenue rose about 4x on a low base and management called battery losses a continuing concern.

532937|2026-03.headline: Kuantum Papers Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 22% QoQ to INR48 crore (15.90% margin) on NSR of INR3,700/MT, despite input cost pressure.
532937|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operational income was INR301 crore, up 4% QoQ, driven by NSR improvement to INR3,700/MT, while input costs rose about INR2,000/MT amid the West Asia conflict. EBITDA reached INR48 crore (margin 15.90%, up 234 bps QoQ) and PAT INR14 crore (margin 4.75%, up 137 bps QoQ). For FY26, revenue fell 1% YoY to INR1,093 crore and EBITDA was INR162 crore (14.80% margin), with NSR down about INR2,000/MT and costs up about INR3,200/MT. Management guided to volume growth to about 2,30,000 MT and EBITDA margin of 18-20% over the next few years, with PM3 upgrade and pulp (DDS) commissioning slated for mid-June to July 2026.

segments.name: Notebook paper
segments.commentary: Share fell from about 22% of sales before the September GST change to about 7-8% now; management intends to exit the segment after machine upgrades, citing reversal of input tax credit at nil GST.

segments.name: Copier, high-end printing, specialty paper
segments.commentary: Copier share is growing steadily; Maplitho and size grades target high-end printing; specialty grades targeted at 20-30% of production volume.

segments.name: Paperboard
segments.commentary: Management noted MIP for paperboard continues with a one-year extension; paperboard was not discussed in detail.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line expected at INR1,400-1,500 crore, rising gradually to INR1,600 crore; FY28 INR1,600-1,700 crore (management's medium-term view: INR1,600-1,700 crore).
Volumes to rise from about 1,62,000-1,63,000 MT to about 2,30,000 MT, a 40-50% increase, at utilisation above 90-95%.
EBITDA margin target of 18-20% over the medium term.
Operating cost reduction of 5-8% of total manufacturing cost once AI/digital projects are fully implemented, expected across machines by FY27-FY28.
Peak long-term debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027, reducing INR100-200 crore a year thereafter; annual repayments of INR170-180 crore over the next 2-3 years.
Remaining capex of about INR125 crore to be spent in FY27; no new capex planned beyond current projects, though another expansion may be considered in about two years.
Tissue paper project deferred, not shelved, until debt is under control.
Wheat straw prices expected to ease after rice sowing starts in early June; Q1 season expected to be lean with pricing pressure.
capex_capacity: PM2 rebuild completed March 2026, capacity raised to 75 TPD; PM1 rebuild in December 2025 added about 20 TPD on average in Q4.
PM3 upgrade delayed due to German imported parts; now planned by mid-June/July 2026 (previously around May).
Displacement Digester System (DDS) for wood pulping under extensive testing, commissioning targeted by mid-June; pulp capacity to come on stream by PM3 commissioning (July).
Two-stage recausticizing plant and 80 TPD synchro sheeter commissioned; overall utilisation above 92% on PM1, PM2 and PM4 (OE levels).
Cost of PM3 upgrade not expected to escalate versus the earlier INR140-150 crore estimate.
demand_pricing: Pricing firmed in Q4 on higher demand, but May price hikes partly reversed; management says it holds prices at about INR69,000-70,000/ton.
Low-priced imports persisted through FY26, lowering domestic prices; West Asia freight disruption reduced import volumes in Q4, with risk of China/Indonesia trade diversion.

Anti-subsidy application expected to be processed by FY-end (March 2027); anti-dumping application on writing and printing paper typically takes 1.5-2 years; MIP for writing/printing paper still under review.
Global pulp prices at about USD600-700/ton, expected to stay in that range given new capacity additions.
Wheat straw prices up about 50-60% YoY, with the fuel-use competition now unwound; wood chip prices broadly stable.
Chemical input costs up about 3-5% for some chemicals; the company is absorbing rather than passing these through.
Dealer network of about 90 committed dealers plus about 20 irregular dealers; Gulf and North African export markets being developed.

qa_highlights.question: Are import pressures visible now, and will they hurt pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes from China and Indonesia did not arrive in Q4 due to West Asia freight disruption; the impact may return later, and the industry is pursuing Gulf export opportunities. Comment restricted to white paper, not paperboard.

qa_highlights.question: Current debt and capex plans for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt was INR720 crore on 31 March 2026; peak debt of INR650-675 crore by end-2027. Remaining capex of about INR125 crore in FY27 and no new capex planned beyond existing projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of PM3 and pulp capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: PM3 delayed due to German parts, now targeted by mid-June; pulp upgrade to come on stream alongside PM3 in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new capacity be absorbed, given the demand environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 95%+ utilisation; cited the dealer network, Gulf and Northern Africa markets, and a 25-30% specialty grade mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: How much opex can be cut from AI and capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5-8% of total manufacturing cost reduction once AI systems are deployed across machines, progressing machine by machine and mill-wide, with completion targeted by FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company refinance or reduce cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Average long-term cost of funds is about 8.5%; management is exploring FCNRB and cheaper funding options. Buybacks are not being considered for now.

risks_watch: Import pressure from China and Indonesia, and dumping, could return once freight normalises; the anti-subsidy outcome is a key dependency.
Ramp-up risk: volumes must rise 40-50% to about 2,30,000 MT, with pulp capacity and PM3 timelines already slipping.
Leverage is high: long-term debt of INR720 crore at about 8.5% average cost, with annual repayments of INR170-180 crore.
Lean season expected in the next 2-3 months with historical pricing dips; management expects reversal around September.
Input costs (chemicals, wheat straw, pulp) remain elevated; the company is absorbing chemical cost increases.
Notebook exit reduces the top line and may affect volume in the near term.
532937|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and medium-term targets, but cautious on near-term pricing and input costs; several answers were corrective or deferred, including the tissue project and the MIP and ADD outcomes. Management was defensive when challenged on capacity absorption and debt.
key_quotes: Encouragingly, pricing began to fir m up in the fourth quarter, supported by higher demand, though was dampened a bit by the cost-led adjustments due to the ongoing West Asia conflict.
So, you can expect the top line to be in the range of INR1,600 crores to INR1,700 crores thereabouts.
And we are not foreseeing any kind of stiff competition, particularly for us.
It's a conscious call not to remain in this segment.

rows.why: PM3 upgrade (INR140 crore, under construction) and DDS pulp commissioning are slated for mid-June to July 2026, lifting volume from about 1,62,000-1,63,000 MT to about 2,30,000 MT (40-50%), though PM3 has already slipped from May on German parts.

rows.why: Volumes guided to about 2,30,000 MT from 1,62,885 MT in FY26 (40-50% up) at 95%+ utilisation, but current utilisation is already above 92% and the ramp depends on PM3 and pulp timelines that have slipped.

rows.why: FY27 revenue guide of INR1,400-1,500 crore is 28-37% above FY26's INR1,093 crore, but it depends on unbuilt volume and the company is absorbing input cost increases with pricing pressure in the lean season.

rows.why: Management expects 5-8% of total manufacturing cost reduction as AI systems roll out machine by machine, with completion targeted by FY27-FY28.

rows.label: Peak debt INR650-675 crore by end-2027, then INR100-200 crore a year lower
rows.why: Long-term debt was INR720 crore on 31 March 2026 with annual repayments of INR170-180 crore; average cost of funds about 8.5%, and FCNRB refinancing is being explored.

rows.label: Gulf and North African export markets
rows.why: Being developed alongside a dealer network of about 90 committed dealers plus about 20 irregular dealers, but no export volume or revenue figures were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating momentum (utilisation above 92%, 18-20% margin target) but cautious on near-term pricing, input costs and import risk, and defensive when challenged on capacity absorption and debt; analysts pushed on capacity absorption, debt and cost of funds.

532937|2026-06.headline: Kuantum Q1 FY27 operational income rose 36% YoY to INR304 crore, but EBITDA was flat at INR40 crore (13.2% margin) as input costs outran price gains.
532937|2026-06.overview: Paper sales volume grew 35% YoY to 42,922 metric tons, and blended NSR improved about INR3,400/ton QoQ. Cost per ton rose about INR4,200 QoQ on raw material, chemical and fuel inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, so EBITDA stayed broadly flat YoY and PAT was INR6 crore. Management cut its FY27 top-line expectation to INR1,300 crore-plus from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore and pushed the 16-18% EBITDA margin target to the year-end. PM3 rebuild completion, pulp capacity additions and anti-dumping applications were the main operational updates.

segments.name: Paper (writing & printing, copier, maplitho)
segments.commentary: Realisation around INR68,000-69,000/ton per management, targeted to reach INR72,000-75,000 in 4-6 months. Specialty grades are just under 20% of mix (18-19% stated), target 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line revised to INR1,300 crore-plus, versus earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore guidance; management said realisations are running below earlier expected levels.
EBITDA margin at least 16-18% by year-end; management says Q3 onwards is when these margins should be visible, not Q2.
FY28 top line expected INR1,400-1,500 crore; FY29-30 conservatively INR1,500 crore at current pricing, INR1,600-1,650 crore if pricing rises to about INR75,000/ton.
Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; scheduled repayments about INR170-175 crore per year for the next 2-3 years; debt to fall below INR300-350 crore within 3 years.
AI-led opex reduction target of 4-5% by March 2028.
Pulp capacity to rise to about 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD.
capex_capacity: DDS (Double Displacement Digester) for wood pulping commissioned in Q1.
Native starch system commissioned on PM2 and PM3.
Folio ream wrapping machine installed in the finishing house.
PM3 shut for major rebuild; management expects commissioning within about a week of the call (mid-August 2026), completing the upgradation programme.
Pulping capacity of about 200 TPD each for agro and wood, said to be sufficient for all four machines.
EC clearance for PM3 upgrade filed and awaited.
Clonal propagation: record 17.28 lakh saplings in the quarter; plantation area about 19,650 acres after adding about 1,300 acres.
demand_pricing: Demand supported by education, publishing and office consumption; management expects demand to stay supportive.
Chinese imports diminishing, attributed mainly to shipping and container cost issues; imported copier/maplitho price seen at $610-620/ton near port.
Anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing and printing paper, covering 40-140 GSM; management hopes for a favourable decision, assumed 5-year duration.
Maplitho hit by inverted duty structure after GST change; management says Kuantum is reducing notebook paper exposure and passing GST losses to customers.
Management says pricing held flat QoQ into Q2 with no discounting; dealer channel inventory described as lean.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance maintained, and what EBITDA margin is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is positive with PM3 commissioning, targeting at least 16-18% EBITDA margin by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak debt and the repayment path?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt about INR760-770 crore; repayments of about INR170-175 crore a year for 2-3 years, with debt below INR300 crore within 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the revenue guidance fall from INR1,400-1,500 crore to INR1,300 crore-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations are running below earlier expected levels and EBITDA margins are strained by West Asia-driven costs; management says figures are conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall while a competitor's rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Punjab-specific raw material cost increases, mainly wheat straw, which it says is easing; it expects a gradual reduction in procurement cost.

qa_highlights.question: What share of cost increase is due to the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the INR4,200/ton cost increase is attributed to West Asia; INR3,400/ton has been passed through in pricing QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will wheat straw prices come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said procurement prices fell in Q2 versus Q1 after negotiations with suppliers, with further easing expected as rice straw and corn cobs arrive in September-October.

risks_watch: Cost pass-through: about INR800/ton of the INR4,200/ton cost rise was not recovered in Q1 price gains; watch whether Q2 NSR and margins recover.
Execution on PM3 commissioning (mid-August) and full-capacity ramp; Q2 is expected to be weak with machine and boiler shutdowns.
Revenue guidance cut and inconsistency with earlier FY28-30 projections.
Q2 seasonally weak demand; management says October onwards is when the industry picks up.
Pending EC clearance for PM3 and pending anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duty decision.
Debt of about INR760-770 crore at peak and interest burden on PAT.

Answers on the guidance gap and FY30 targets were partly contradictory and hard to reconcile.
key_quotes: We should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.
Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum.
Nobody could have imagined like a war starting in a part of the world and impacting sort of pricing here in India.
Right now, our contribution from specialty paper is just under 20%.

532940|2026-03.headline: J. Kumar FY26 revenue rose 1% to INR5,723 crore with EBITDA flat at INR823 crore; management guides 15% top-line growth in FY27.
532940|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a flat year: consolidated revenue rose 1% to INR5,723 crore, EBITDA was INR823 crore (14.4% margin) and PAT was INR387 crore, with management attributing the slowdown to external factors that delayed execution. Q4 FY26 revenue fell 3% YoY to INR1,585 crore and PAT fell 5% to INR110 crore. Order book stood at INR18,554 crore on 31 March 2026, and management says inflows since 1 April 2026 have taken it to about INR25,000 crore including L1. Management guides FY27 revenue and PAT growth of about 15%, EBITDA margin of 15-16%, and new order intake of INR9,000-10,000 crore.

financial_highlights.change: -3% vs INR1,633 crore in Q4 FY25
-5% vs INR235 crore; 14.4% in Q4 FY25
-5% vs INR114 crore; 7% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: Unbilled revenue INR578 crore; mobilisation advance INR706 crore; retention INR464 crore

segments.name: Order book mix (31 March 2026)
segments.commentary: Elevated corridors and flyovers about 51%, others about 20%, road and tunnel projects about 18%, metro (elevated and underground) about 11%.

segments.name: Chennai and GMLR projects
segments.commentary: Chennai casting yard fully operational and segment casting started; GMLR has cast over 3.5 km of tunnel, and management expects roughly 20-30% output from Chennai and GMLR in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth about 15%, implying crossing INR6,500 crore; management says upside is possible but is committing to 15%.
FY27 PAT growth about 15%; PAT margin about 7%.
EBITDA margin targeted to rise from 14-15% to 15-16%, with further basis-point gains over 6-8 quarters.
FY27 new order intake target INR9,000-10,000 crore; management says it will cross INR10,000 crore, with INR15,000-20,000 crore of projects to bid in FY27.
Capex of INR200-250 crore per year for FY27 and FY28 including incremental capex and GMLR/Chennai balance.
Management says it is 'one year behind' its earlier INR7,500 crore FY27 revenue target (given when the dollar was INR75) and now expects it in FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR280 crore in FY25 and about INR400 crore in FY26; quarterly depreciation rose to about INR66 crore in Q4 FY26 from INR40-45 crore, and management expects it to stay elevated.

GMLR: TBM assembled; first machine in advanced assembly with SAT targeted around June 2026 and drilling to start then; second TBM about 1.5 months behind. The TBM is financed by a 3-year term loan, about 10% repaid so far, and no major additional TBM capex is planned.
Chennai: foundation and substructure work underway, casting yard operational. Management says the INR500 crore Chennai flyover project is about 50% complete and on schedule.

Versova-Dahisar Coastal Road Package B: approvals largely received, mangrove cutting about 10% done, over 100 piles and 14-15 foundations completed, 7-8 piers cast; a 6-7 km connector toward Filmcity is also in scope.
Vizag investment property (originally a PSL asset): INR90 crore of INR106 crore loan repaid; management expects the balance to be exited by Q2.
demand_pricing: Inflows since 1 April 2026 to 19 May 2026 about INR6,300 crore (LOA about INR4,500 crore, L1 about INR1,770 crore; L1 expected to convert in 15-30 days). Order book is about INR25,000 crore including these, versus INR18,554 crore at 31 March.

Maharashtra pipeline: Metro Lines 5, 10, 13 and 14, Uttan-Virar elevated corridor (over INR50,000-60,000 crore), tenders expected in 3-6 months. Management cites about INR1 lakh crore of Maharashtra awards expected within about 12 months.

Management said the Q1 margin included a one-off of about INR46 crore (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore cost) from the KNR Palani cash surplus EPC claim, and that underlying EBITDA was about 5.5%. Working capital days rose to 133 from 78 at March 2026, and consolidated net debt-to-equity rose to 0.9 from 0.49. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200-2,300 crore at 8-9% EBITDA, with a stronger FY28 and new mining and HAM execution from Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Includes one-off from KNR Palani/Ramagiri sale proceeds

financial_highlights.value: INR46 crore net (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore expense)

segments.name: HAM (Hybrid Annuity)
segments.commentary: About 70% of Q1 revenue. Ramanattukara-Valanchery and Valanchery-Kappirikkad at 100%; Marripudi-Somavarappadu ~86%; Magadi-Somwarpet ~91%; Mysore-Kushalnagara Packages 4 and 5 at ~20% and ~18%. INR595 crore of INR805 crore revised equity invested.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: About 25% of Q1 revenue. Water pipeline revenue was only INR7 crore in Q1; INR830 crore pipeline order book, guided INR300-400 crore FY27 execution.

segments.name: Irrigation
segments.commentary: About 3% of Q1 revenue. Unexecuted irrigation book ~INR800 crore; INR825 crore of irrigation book already recognised but unbilled; guided ~INR200 crore FY27 execution. Telangana Package 4 receivables ~INR1,300 crore, total irrigation receivables ~INR1,450 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue INR2,200-2,300 crore (10-15% above FY26's ~INR2,000 crore), with EBITDA ~8-9%.
Q3 and Q4 FY27 EBITDA expected at ~11-12%; FY28 revenue above INR3,000 crore at ~11-12% EBITDA (average 12-13% cited in one answer).
FY29 EBITDA margin guided at ~8-9% (Q3/Q4 ~10-11%).
FY27 order inflow target INR8,000-10,000 crore (NHAI, irrigation, state government works).
FY27 capex INR350-400 crore including mining; Kusmunda mining capex ~INR400-450 crore in FY27 per one answer, which conflicts with the company-level figure.

Expects irrigation recovery of INR400-500 crore in FY27 from Telangana, with ~INR650 crore outstanding on Package 4 and a revised estimate of over INR700 crore pending government sanction (5-6 months).
Additional HAM equity of INR210 crore (INR125 crore FY27, INR85 crore FY28), plus possibly ~INR510 crore for Chennai ECR and Telangana HAM.
Buyback under consideration; board decision pending, no size disclosed.
capex_capacity: Kusmunda coal mining (Chhattisgarh, SECL LOA, INR3,361 crore excluding GST, 8 years, with JV partner Sushee Infra): appointed date expected early September 2026 after rains; equipment INR500-600 crore; 100-tonne dumpers due by end-November; Q1 capex nil to INR14 crore.
Banhardih mine (Jharkhand, older award, 5-year contract): only one forest stage cleared; land acquisition 5-6 months; start ~8-10 months away, so likely FY28; equipment INR300-400 crore.
Surface miners cost ~INR13 crore each; four needed initially, up to five if delays.
Mining equipment financing via Caterpillar and Komatsu two-year buyback arrangements (~75% residual value cited), reducing depreciation burden.
demand_pricing: Order book INR8,667 crore excluding 2 new HAM projects and the mining project; INR15,234 crore including them. Mix: roads 38%, irrigation 11%, pipeline 6%, mining 45%.
Client mix: 71% third-party (46% central government, 24% state government, 1% private) and 29% captive HAM.
Order book executable over 3-3.5 years excluding mining; mining 5 and 8 years.
Unbilled order book ~INR1,220 crore (irrigation INR825 crore, others ~INR400 crore). Somvarappadu unexecuted ~INR100 crore vs INR153 crore last quarter.
Railways: FY27 central railway capex INR2.93 lakh crore; Andhra Pradesh railway allocation INR10,134 crore. Metro/MRTS and battery energy storage also evaluated.

Current L1 position ~INR1,500 crore, LOA not yet issued (Chennai and Hyderabad). Bidding in Odisha elevated metro lost on unhealthy pricing; UPEIDA excluded due to greenfield expressway experience requirement.
NHAI FY27 plan to award 54 projects (2,444 km, ~INR1.8 lakh crore); Q1 NHAI awards ~107 km vs ~638 km executed.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 and FY28 execution and revenue look, and when do the two new HAM projects reach appointed date?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue guided at INR2,200-2,300 crore (10-15% above ~INR2,000 crore in FY26), with ECR Chennai, Telangana Mahabubnagar and Kusmunda starting; FY28 targeted above INR3,000 crore. The two new HAM projects are expected to reach appointed date in Q3, and the older Banhardih mine is likely FY28 given 8-10 months to start.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are targeted for FY27, FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 margins to be similar to Q1's; Q3 and Q4 expected at about 11-12%. FY28 average cited at 12-13%, and FY29 at about 8-9% (Q3/Q4 about 10-11%).

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 15% EBITDA margin a one-off, and what is the underlying margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Q1 included about INR90 crore cash surplus EPC claim including GST from the investor deal; net one-off of INR46 crore (INR76 crore revenue less INR30 crore expense). Excluding it, EBITDA margin is around 5.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much irrigation recovery and Telangana Package 4 payment is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management discussed monthly instalments of about INR70-90 crore, with about INR650 crore outstanding on Package 4 and a revised estimate above INR700 crore pending government sanction over 5-6 months. Analyst's INR400-500 crore FY27 recovery estimate was accepted as expected by management.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed for the Kusmunda and Banhardih mines, and how will depreciation look?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 capex was about INR14 crore. Kusmunda equipment INR500-600 crore; FY27 Kusmunda capex about INR400-450 crore, Banhardih about INR200 crore in FY27 per one answer. Company-level FY27 capex INR350-400 crore. Caterpillar and Komatsu dumpers carry two-year buybacks with about 75% residual value; surface miners and coal equipment are held five to eight years. Management did not give a depreciation figure and targets PAT of 6%-plus on mining.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the buyback and dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback under consideration; a conclusion meeting is pending and the Board will decide. No size, mechanism or percentage disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and expected mining and irrigation revenue for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 revenue split: HAM 70%, EPC 25%, irrigation 3%. FY27 irrigation about INR200 crore from ~INR800 crore unexecuted book; pipeline INR300-400 crore; mining about INR150 crore in FY27 (INR20-40 crore slippage risk) and about INR400 crore in FY28 from Kusmunda, with Banhardih possibly INR500 crore a year if it starts.

qa_highlights.question: What unbilled order book and Somvarappadu and Mysore-Kushalnagara exposure exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbilled order book about INR1,220 crore (irrigation INR825 crore, others about INR400 crore). Somvarappadu unexecuted about INR100 crore versus INR153 crore last quarter. Mysore-Kushalnagara Packages 4 and 5 are expected to be completed by April-May 2027, with partial COD by December on land available.

risks_watch: Q1 margin of 15% is inflated by a one-off of about INR46 crore net; underlying margin about 5.5%, so H2 guidance of 11-12% EBITDA depends on HAM and mining ramp-up.
Telangana Package 4 recovery: about INR650 crore outstanding plus a revised estimate above INR700 crore pending government sanction over 5-6 months; receivables total about INR1,450 crore irrigation.
Working capital days rose to 133 from 78 at March 2026 and consolidated net debt-to-equity rose to 0.9 from 0.49, with consolidated debt at INR1,975 crore.

Kusmunda mining start depends on appointed date (expected early September) amid monsoon haul-road delays; 100-tonne dumpers due by end-November. Banhardih timing uncertain (likely FY28) due to forest and land approvals.

Mining capex inconsistencies on the call: FY27 Kusmunda capex cited as INR400-450 crore in one answer versus company-level INR350-400 crore; mining depreciation and EBITDA not yet quantified by management.

Order inflow target INR8,000-10,000 crore for FY27 against Q1 NHAI awards of about 107 km versus about 638 km executed; L1 of about INR1,500 crore awaiting LOA; UPEIDA excluded for lack of greenfield expressway experience; battery storage bids seen as risky.
Additional HAM equity of INR210 crore plus possibly about INR510 crore for Chennai ECR and Telangana HAM; buyback size and mechanism still undecided.
key_quotes: So FY27 will be this. And as far as FY28 is concerned, definitely, that year should be the good year because whatever the projects are there, projects will completely start in FY28.
So net INR46 crores has been considered in the EBITDA, as a one-off.
Around 5.5% is there.
Yes, sir. Buyback, we are considering, sir. We'll come back on it.

532953|2026-03.headline: V-Guard Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and PAT 23% to INR112 crore, with FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.8%.
532953|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was strong, with revenue up 14.1% YoY to INR1,755 crore and EBITDA excluding other income up 19.3% to INR171 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 7% and EBITDA rose 2.6% to INR527 crore. Growth came almost entirely in the second half after a weak summer in the first half. Management is pursuing price hikes of roughly 13% to offset input cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict, with about 75% landed so far. Net cash rose to INR231 crore and the board recommended a final dividend of INR1.5 per share.

segments.name: Electronics (Stabilizers, UPS, Inverters, Batteries)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 22.3% YoY with all categories growing; about 3% of growth was price and the balance volume, per management. Solar inverters are a newer line, not yet at INR500 crore.

segments.name: Electrical (Wires, Pumps, Switchgears, Modular Switches)
segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor; Q4 revenue grew 15.9% YoY. Wires face rising competition from new entrants, though management sees the category as low-margin and scale-dependent.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (Fans, Water Heaters, Kitchen Appliances, Air Coolers)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 4.1% YoY; fans and air coolers declined while water heaters and kitchen grew strongly. TPW fans are short of supply due to a plastic raw material shortage.

segments.name: Sunflame (Kitchen Appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.6% YoY; the CSD business is still slowing, but non-CSD grew about 16%. GT integration is complete and sales integration is still underway.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 10-12% volume growth and 1-2% price growth (about 15% total) over time, with higher price growth likely in FY27 due to cost inflation.
EBITDA margin: management says at least 10% is the target for the next year if summer is good, but declined to commit to 11-12%; cited prolonged high cost as a reason for caution.
Expects a good growth year for Consumer Durables on a low base, and a strong start to FY27 given Q4 momentum and a supportive summer forecast.
Cost discipline: no major manpower increases planned; variable pay will fall if top and bottom line targets are missed.
Price increases: about 75% of the required ~13% price hike landed so far; the remaining ~25% is expected as high-cost inventory flows in during May-June.
Raw material supply secured through June for most items; sulfuric acid and certain TPW fan plastics remain tight.
capex_capacity: Management said bulk of new capacity investment is done and ramp-up is under way; capex will still absorb some cash in FY27.
Company spent close to INR300-400 crore over the last 8 years on plants and manufacturing integration.
BLDC is about 40% of ceiling fan sales; BLDC chimneys launched; BLDC mixer grinders not yet launched.
Lighting entry is still work in progress, with launch targeted around early next quarter (Q1 FY27).
No acquisitions planned; any opportunity would be assessed case by case.
demand_pricing: Input costs up 8-13% across representative categories; management says the West Asia conflict has caused commodity inflation and supply shocks, worse than the Ukraine-war period.
Price hikes of about 10-12% (some up to 15-20% industry-wide) face retailer pushback; the company gave case-by-case support in regions where summer has not started.
South India summer demand is strong (sales started early March/April); non-South is mixed due to rain, with East a key market for summer products.
Channel financing covers about 35% of the debtor book (customer-linked, not category-linked); collections were strong in the March quarter.
Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue; no impact seen so far, with summer in Kerala supportive. Non-South contributed 48% of FY26 revenue; South grew 16.2% and non-South 11.8% in Q4.
Competition: wire entrants and lighting peers are entering; management expects consolidation to be slow and sees the top 4-5 brands per category as the survivors.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken across segments, and is another round needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs up 8-13%; about 75% of the required price increase has landed, with the remaining 25% expected as high-cost inventory arrives in May-June.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Kitchen Appliances segment come out of its slump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes demand is improving, with traction for both V-Guard and Sunflame; Sunflame now uses V-Guard's sales network.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kerala softness affecting demand after March?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact seen so far; Kerala is about 15-16% of revenue and summer there has been supportive. Q1 is primarily a summer quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins reach double digits in one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 FY26 EBITDA was about 9.5%; management is confident of at least 10% once raw material prices normalise, but declined to guide 11-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar business size and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar is below INR500 crore, about 36 months old; management expects it to be among the larger categories in 3-4 years, focused on residential B2C.

qa_highlights.question: Is raw material availability a risk to production?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfuric acid and polymers are tight; supply is locked up for about a month or more, and management sees no supply challenge through Q1.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation from the West Asia conflict; about 25% of the required price hike is still pending and could face pushback.
Weak non-South summer start; East market is key for summer products and any slip would hurt Q1 FY27 volumes.
Shortage of TPW fan plastic and sulfuric acid could cap output; management expects supply to be about 105 units against 110 demanded.
Rising competition in wires from a large new entrant at the end of 2026 and lighting peers.
Sunflame CSD decline and the pace of benefits from sales integration (expected over the next three quarters); the NPD pipeline lands in H2 FY26 onwards.
Channel inventory is mixed: ceiling fans well stocked after the December 2025 BEE star-rating transition; TPW fans out of stock.
532953|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the business and Q4 momentum, but cautious on margins and near-term inflation. Management declined to commit beyond at least 10% EBITDA margin and said it would reassess after a couple of quarters.

So far we have navigated these challenges well, which reflects the inherent resilience of the business.
But I wouldn't say 11%, 12%, I would say at least 10% is what we would like to expect there.
We have landed most of the pricing action and I think most companies have announced and taken pricing action.

rows.why: Lighting entry is targeted for launch around Q1 FY27 and BLDC mixer grinders are planned but not yet launched, with Sunflame NPD pipeline landing from H2 FY26 onwards.

rows.why: About 75% of the required ~13% price increase has landed, with the remaining ~25% expected as high-cost inventory flows in during May-June, though retailers are pushing back on 10-12% hikes.

rows.label: Strong South summer demand and Q4 momentum
rows.why: South grew 16.2% in Q4 and summer sales started early March/April; management expects a strong start to FY27, though non-South is mixed and East is key for summer products.

rows.label: Variable pay linked to targets; no major manpower increases
rows.why: No major manpower increases are planned and variable pay falls if top and bottom-line targets are missed, which cushions margin if volumes slip.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q4 momentum, South summer demand and the path to at least 10% EBITDA margin, but cautious on input cost inflation, the pending 25% of price hikes and declined to guide 11-12%; analysts pushed on margin timing and price hike pushback.

532953|2026-06.headline: V-Guard Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.4%.
532953|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore, with about 14% price and 9% volume contribution per management's blended split. EBITDA excluding other income rose 54.5% to INR191 crore, and PAT rose 76% to INR130 crore. Gross margin held at 36.9%, flat YoY, as management says roughly 75-80% of input cost inflation has been passed through. Management raised FY27 growth expectations to above 15% and reaffirmed a 9-10% EBITDA margin, while noting wires volumes were nearly flat under a large price increase.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR155 crore a year ago

segments.name: Electronics (stabilizers, UPS, solar)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY with all major categories contributing; solar is growing fastest on a small base, and solar pumps for Maharashtra government are only a couple of crore so far.

segments.name: Electricals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 27.7% YoY, aided by higher copper prices; wires saw very high price growth with near-flat volumes, while ex-wires grew at high double digits and switchgear, modular switches and pumps grew volumes robustly.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (fans, water heaters, kitchen, air coolers)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.2% YoY; induction cooktops spiked, other kitchen categories grew healthily, fans grew reasonably (pedestal fans short on inventory), and air coolers lost share due to weak North demand and competitor price delays.

segments.name: Sunflame
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18.3% YoY on a low base; management says integration is complete and a sales acceleration programme has started, with margin recovery expected to be more gradual than top-line recovery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 15%, with management saying it may be 'a bit more than 15%' given price growth; no specific number given.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 9-10% ('we should be okay this year in terms of margins').
Long-term target of 15% growth, with normal-year mix of 10-12% volume and 2-3% price growth.
Capex to average INR150-170 crore per year over the next two years, below the earlier INR200-250 crore range.
Advertising spend to reach about 2.5% of revenue for FY27, with spending resumed from around May 15.
Pricing actions about 80-85% complete; some smaller categories still need price increases in the current quarter, and management does not expect large further hikes.
Wires competitive intensity expected to slow growth for some unorganised-sector players by 1-2% vs market, with no major impact in the first one to two years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance revised: INR150-170 crore per year on average for the next two years, versus the earlier INR200-250 crore range referenced by the analyst.
Own manufacturing now above 65% of products (previously sourced), a key driver of gross margin improvement.
Investment phase in capability (technology, systems, R&D, renewables, lighting) expected to last another two to three years before plateauing.
Lighting launch planned in FY27; solar rooftop next-generation battery (BESS) launch planned in the next two to three months.
Gegadyne (battery start-up) has moved from R&D to commercial supply to small customers; V-Guard may source batteries from it.
demand_pricing: Pricing: management cited a blended split of about 14% price and 9% volume within 22-23% revenue growth; category price increases range from 5% to 18%, with some categories cited up to 30%.
Wires: very large price increases led to near-zero volume growth as customers deferred purchases; value growth held up and margins were maintained.
Copper purchase mix shifted to roughly 95% domestic from 70-80% earlier, which helped working capital through supplier credit.
Management described the 12-14% price increase over four months as unprecedented since 2006 and said consumers have accepted it so far.
Air coolers lost share as some competitors delayed price increases and the North zone was weak.
Solar rooftop: focus is B2C residential and small SMEs; BESS seen as the next large opportunity at about INR1.5-2 lakh per home.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 22-23% growth is price vs volume, and how much of the input inflation has been passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended growth split is about 14% price and 9% volume; about 80-85% of pricing actions are complete and roughly 75-80% of inflation has been passed through, with the gross margin expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why is South growing faster than non-South for the fourth quarter in a row?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it mainly to weather: South had a good summer while North was disrupted by rain. It also said it took pricing ahead of competitors in non-South markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex guidance still INR2-2.5 billion a year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Capex is expected to average INR150-170 crore a year over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth and margins be higher than the medium-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be more than 15%, with the 15% figure kept as the long-term aim. EBITDA margin is expected at 9-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is payables so high on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-off: copper purchases shifted to domestic suppliers who give credit, instead of imports paid by LC, and payables are expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Why not gain share in wires by passing on less price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wires are a commoditised, utilitarian product with low margins, so a price war would be lose-lose and hard to end.

risks_watch: Wires price war from new entrants and a possible festive-season launch; wire volumes near zero and customer deferment.
Sustainability of working capital gains, as the high payables are described as one-off and net cash of INR670 crore may normalise.
Sunflame margin recovery is expected to be slow given pricing transmission lags in CSD and non-South general trade.
Further commodity volatility from the West Asia conflict and shipping constraints; management says a few smaller categories still need price action.
Ad spend at 2.5% for FY27 vs 2.2% in Q1, and the budget was set on January prices, not current input costs.
Cost base has risen sharply over five years; management expects extended investment for two to three more years.

Cautious and evasive on categories, state-level data and wire-category volumes, which were not disclosed. Management is wary of predicting the FY27 growth rate given volatile commodity prices.
key_quotes: We have delivered double-digit EBITDA margin this quarter.
So in a normal environment, yes, we should grow at 10% to 12% volume growth and 2% to 3% price growth.
So the problem with this price war is that you will start it, but you won't be able to end it.

532967|2026-03.headline: Kiri Industries Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs.241 crore, but reported EBITDA was hit by Rs.114 crore of non-cash year-end adjustments.
532967|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 29% YoY to Rs.241 crore, with management citing volume recovery, better dye intermediate realisations and lower legal costs. Management said adjusted EBITDA was about Rs.35 crore, but Rs.114 crore of non-cash closing-period mark-to-market adjustments were booked, which weighed on reported EBITDA. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 22% to Rs.251 crore and finance cost fell to Rs.8 crore from Rs.54 crore a year earlier. The DyStar award was monetised in FY26 and the copper and fertiliser project (Indo Asia Copper) moved into engineering, ordering and civil works, with commercial operations guided from April 2027 to March 2029.

Debt: minimal debt in FY27 (under Rs.1,000 crore); capex debt of about Rs.4,000-5,000 crore and working capital of Rs.3,000-5,000 crore in FY28, taking total debt to Rs.8,000-9,000 crore. Expected interest rate 8.5-9%, with a three-year principal moratorium.
Government incentives of about 30-35% of eligible capex over 10 years, or roughly Rs.3,000-3,500 crore a year, are in final approval stage.

demand_pricing: Management sees China's tightening of key dye intermediates from environmental compliance and production curbs as supportive of Indian producers' realisations.
Textile customers (over 95% of dyes and chemicals customers) are extending payments, which lengthens Kiri's payables; average payable cycle quoted as 90-120 days.
Management said copper will remain import-dependent until 2030-2035 despite domestic capacity additions, with EV and AI data-centre demand rising.
Secondary copper capacity additions in India are linked to global availability of ingots and blister as exporting countries ban concentrate exports; scrap supply is also rising domestically.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said operations start unit by unit from FY27-28, with Rs.40,000 crore-plus revenue cited for the project at current pricing.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.150 crore has been paid, on the view that most of the award is a judicial capital receipt rather than taxable.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Rs.114 crore adjustment booked and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it relates to mark-to-market on temporary parking of surplus funds in debt, equity and hybrid instruments within India, and it will not recur every quarter or year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest rate and moratorium on the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected rate 8.5-9%, with principal repayment starting three years after drawdown and interest serviced from day one.

qa_highlights.answer: No dividend this year and none to be declared; buyback has not been decided and cash is being retained to fund growth.

532967|2026-06.headline: Kiri Industries Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 63% YoY to INR 295 crore, with PAT of INR 270 crore driven mainly by INR 284 crore other income.
532967|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 63% YoY to INR 295 crore on realisation-led growth in dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals, with standalone material margin at 31.9% versus 23.5% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA was only INR 17 crore (5.86% margin), so PAT of INR 270 crore was largely a function of INR 284 crore other income, mainly treasury gains and inter-corporate loan interest. Consolidated revenue rose 55% to INR 312 crore with EBITDA of INR 37 crore (7.84%), and the group is substantially debt-free after repaying Claronex Holdings' borrowings. The copper and fertiliser project moved into structured construction, with financial closure still incomplete (over 50% of debt commitments received).

segments.name: Dyes, dyes intermediates and basic chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Realisations rose across Reactive Dyes, Vinyl Sulphone, H-Acid and certain basic chemicals; management said H-Acid prices are INR 800-900/unit versus INR 350-400 earlier. Average capacity utilisation was about 60% last quarter, targeted at 70-75% for FY27 if markets support.

segments.name: Lonsen Kiri (associate, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 21 crore to consolidated profit in Q1 FY27. Management cited a JV result of about INR 71 crore EBITDA and INR 51 crore PAT on INR 368 crore revenue, as referenced by an analyst; Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, with 60-70% of JV raw materials sourced from Kiri.

segments.commentary: Total project capital estimated at close to INR 12,000 crore, with INR 1,400 crore deployed to date, all equity so far. Downstream copper tube, rod and refinery phases are planned for Q1 FY28, FY28 and Q3 FY29 respectively.

guidance_outlook: Copper tube plant (35 KT) expected operational June 2027; 2.25 lakh tonne CCR rod plant (8 mm) expected August-September 2027, both stable by January 2028, using imported Japanese LME-grade cathodes.
Part refinery of 1.75 lakh tonnes (anode to cathode) targeted around January 2028, with scrap melting furnace by December 2027-January 2028.
Copper foil trial production targeted around March 2028 (10 KT Phase 1, 40 KT ambition under ECMS scheme); smelter, sulphuric acid plant and fertiliser balance of plant expected Q1 2029.
First copper revenue expected around end Q1 FY28 (May-June 2027); majority of copper operating revenue expected in FY30.
Management said the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore no longer holds; the numbers are dynamic and depend on vendor timelines.
Debt repayment expected to start in 2029 given moratorium; cash flow expected to ramp stepwise over FY28-FY30.
No dividend declared; no Board decision yet, per management.
capex_capacity: Total copper project capital estimated at close to INR 12,000 crore, excluding additional infrastructure spend; outflow expected over the next two years.
Financial closure incomplete; more than 50% of debt commitments received, balance in process, with complete closure hoped within a few months.
Copper concentrate: MoUs of about 1 million tonnes secured against about 1.5 million tonnes needed at full utilisation; firm contracts typically converted around October each year.
Captive jetty (for bulk imports of copper concentrate, phosphate and ammonia), desalination facility, raw material conveying system and power infrastructure in progress; site near Pipavav Port.
MCB Copper-Gold mine: development not started; 70% off-take structured for Kiri, but Celsius is contesting the off-take in court.
demand_pricing: Reactive Dyes, Vinyl Sulphone, H-Acid and certain basic chemical prices strengthened in Q1 on tighter global supply and Chinese environmental compliance measures.
Demand is mixed across product categories; input costs rose with crude oil-linked raw materials, with pass-through supporting margins.

Management said existing H-Acid and Vinyl Sulphone capacity could drive about INR 2,000 crore of dyes revenue at 75-80% utilisation if current prices hold, versus about INR 1,200 crore cited as the current base.
Copper: management sees sales as not a constraint because India consumes about 1.8 million tonnes a year with about two-thirds imported; customer quality approvals still required.
Management said sustaining margins depends on passing through input cost movements.

qa_highlights.question: Will the earlier FY28 revenue guidance of INR 20,000-25,000 crore still hold given staggered tube and rod commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 20,000-25,000 crore FY28 figure does not hold; projections are moving with vendor delivery timelines. It added that sales are not a constraint since the output would substitute imports.

qa_highlights.question: When will copper revenue start and when will it be fully ramped?
qa_highlights.answer: First copper revenue expected around May-June 2027 (Q1 FY28), with commercial operations from Q2 FY28; majority of operating revenue expected in FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Kiri's standalone profitability low when Lonsen Kiri earns strong margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kiri supplies raw materials to the JV, which captures finished-product margins; the JV also makes products Kiri does not, so the combined value chain should be assessed. Lonsen Kiri is operated by Kiri management with no plan to replicate its products in Kiri.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to raise equity to reduce debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity dilution is a plan B option with investor interest tested, but the Board prefers deferred dilution after execution to capture more value. Debt repayment begins in 2029 due to moratorium.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the MCB Copper-Gold mine and the off-take?
qa_highlights.answer: Development has not started; design complete. Shareholder disputes and Celsius litigation are ongoing and sub judice, so management declined to speculate and said Kiri remains a lender.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a stake sale or MMCI interest?
qa_highlights.answer: No current talks on a 40% stake sale in Lonsen Kiri. Management said it would be 100% interested in an MMCI mine stake, subject to the litigation outcome.

key_quotes: So, that INR 20,000 crore-INR 25,000 crore of revenue in 2027-2028 doesn't hold. Let me first clarify that.
A complete financial closure has not been achieved yet. We are there on the debt raising. More than 50% commitments have been received.
But we continue to provide our commitment to the project. We continue to support the project.

532976|2026-06.headline: Jai Balaji Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore; adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore, PAT up 21% to INR85 crore.
532976|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,683 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 46% to INR154 crore (about 9% margin) and PAT up 21% to INR85 crore (about 5% margin), attributed to price normalisation and operational efficiency. Ferroalloy and pig iron realisations rose sharply YoY, while DI pipe demand stayed subdued on slow government ordering and fund releases. Management declined to give volume or EBITDA guidance, citing uncertainty, but said pipe prices are at the bottom and cannot fall further. Expansion capex was revised up to INR1,112 crore from about INR1,000 crore, with completion expected by Q3 FY27 and the balance by end-2026.

segments.name: Ductile iron pipes (DI)
segments.commentary: About 15% of Q1 turnover; utilisation about 30% of the enhanced 5.5 lakh tpa capacity. Order book about four months at current dispatch rate. Management said pipe margins were similar to pig iron margins in Q1.

segments.name: Specialised ferroalloys
segments.commentary: About 27% of revenue; utilisation above 80% in the last quarter. Ferroalloy prices up 46% YoY. Management guided a long-term margin of 15-20%, and exports go to more than 42 countries.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: About 19% of revenue; realisations up 16% YoY.

segments.commentary: Sponge iron 7.4%, billets 3.5%, coke about 7%, scrap and fines about 1% of revenue. Sponge iron and billet realisations were broadly stable.

qa_highlights.question: When will increased government spending translate into DI pipe dispatches?

qa_highlights.question: Will pricing pressure persist given competition?

qa_highlights.question: Can you give DI pipe EBITDA per tonne guidance?

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of specialised ferroalloys versus conventional steel?

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex rise to about INR1,100 crore?

qa_highlights.question: What is the DI pipe order book?

533023|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,197 crore (+15.2% YoY), but margins compressed on material cost and a pricing lag from the Middle East conflict.
533023|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR 1,197 crore, the highest single quarter, up 15.2% YoY, with PBT of INR 196.6 crore (+16.4%) and PAT of INR 146.3 crore (+15.5%). FY26 revenue was INR 4,302 crore (+9.2%), PBT INR 693 crore (+13.9%) and PAT INR 517 crore (+12.2%). Management attributed the Q4 margin fall (about 230 bps QoQ) to material cost increases from supply constraints and the Middle East conflict, plus a January salary increase, with customer price recovery still under negotiation. The board approved a 5:1 bonus issue and a final dividend of INR 4 per share post bonus.

segments.name: OE (original equipment)
segments.commentary: Q4 OE sales grew about 25% YoY; FY26 OE sales grew 17.5-17.6% to INR 1,978 crore, outperforming an industry where >6t vehicle production rose 16.6% to 463,000 units. Q4 >6t production hit a record 151,000 units (+26.9%).

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q4 aftermarket grew about 21% YoY to INR 151 crore; FY26 revenue INR 583-584 crore (+15.5-15.6%). Network expanded by 51 distributor branches and 14 service centres.

segments.name: Exports (goods)
segments.commentary: Q4 exports fell about 6% YoY per the call, with Europe up about 6% and the Americas down about 22%; FY26 exports INR 1,025 crore (-11.1%). Management guided to moderate improvement, with early US recovery signs in Q4.

segments.name: Export services (engineering)
segments.commentary: Export of services grew 22.5% YoY in Q4 and 15.4% for FY26, driven by engineering work for global centres; service income for FY26 was INR 509 crore (+10%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating margin expected to be broadly flat, with at most single-digit growth; management was cautious given the Middle East conflict and government calls for expense control.
FY27 capex guided at INR 180-190 crore, covering new product capex plus replacements and upgrades.
April and May 2026 volumes were described as better than prior years, with Q1 expected to be a good quarter.
Final dividend of INR 4 per share post bonus; bonus issue 5:1 with record date 24 June 2026 and deemed allotment 25 June 2026, subject to approvals; AGM and dividend record date 10 July 2026.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR 180-190 crore, split between new products and replacement/upgrade spend.

Oragadam multidivisional plant: new lines for crankshaft machining, ASP cartridges and vacuum pump commissioned; management said Mahindra World City utilisation is near peak and further expansion will be at Oragadam.
Jamshedpur rainwater harvesting pond of 1,200 kL to meet about 40% of plant water needs; Ambattur organic waste converter commissioned.
Assembly capabilities strengthened at Jamshedpur and Lucknow; OMA maturity assessment completed with a good score across Ambattur, Mahindra World City, Lucknow and Jamshedpur.
demand_pricing: Q4 margin fell about 230 bps QoQ on higher material costs (aluminium up from about INR 233/kg to INR 274/kg, roughly 18% of material cost) and a January salary increase; price recovery talks with customers are ongoing and lag costs.
ESC is voluntarily fitted in POL/tanker trucks today; regulation kicks in from October 2027 for vehicles above 6t, and management expects value per vehicle to rise as ESC penetration increases.
ADAS: management has won full-suite business from 2 OEMs; discussions are ongoing with most other OEMs, with several competitors also engaged.
Management said OEMs are increasingly splitting ESC and AEBS/ADAS across partners, while AEBS/ADAS (5 mandated features) is typically sourced from a single partner.
Q3 to Q4 value per vehicle drop was attributed to one-off retrospective selling price variances recognised in Q3; excluding them, value per vehicle was roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall about 230 bps QoQ, and what is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher material costs from supply constraints and the Middle East conflict, plus a January salary increase, with no one-offs. FY27 margin is expected to be broadly flat with single-digit growth, with caution on the macro outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA growth lag revenue growth in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increases from the war and commodity prices came ahead of customer price recoveries, creating a timing lag that management expects to correct over time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q4 segment growth rates and blended export decline?
qa_highlights.answer: OE grew about 25%, aftermarket about 21%, exports fell about 6%, and export services rose 22.5%. Europe grew about 6%, the Americas fell about 22%, and the blended export decline was about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of diesel price hikes on demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher diesel prices would hit freight rates and truck utilisation, which could slow vehicle purchases with a lag. Replacement demand for inefficient old trucks could offset this.

qa_highlights.question: How does ADAS and AEBS sourcing work with ESC?
qa_highlights.answer: ESC and ADAS can be sourced from separate suppliers, but AEBS and ADAS are typically awarded to one partner able to demonstrate all 5 mandated features.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for US exports and the FY30 India localisation target?
qa_highlights.answer: The US export gap versus two years ago is still about 20%, though US vehicle production has risen for four months. Management said new RFQs are coming in and the group's India growth commitment stands.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and commodity cost inflation (aluminium) squeezing margins until customer price recoveries are agreed.
Diesel price hike may reduce freight rates and truck utilisation, delaying vehicle purchases.
US export volumes still about 20% below two years ago; Americas down about 22% in Q4.
Timing of ESC and ADAS mandate from October 2027 and the pace of further OEM ADAS awards.
Q3 one-off selling price variances distorted value per vehicle; watch the Q1 FY27 reading.
Supplier constraints and gas shortages seen earlier in FY26 could recur.

533023|2026-06.headline: ZF CV India Q1 FY27: Total income up 5.7% to ₹1,101.8 cr; PAT fell 14.7% to ₹104.5 cr on a high base FX gain, while aftermarket rose 15.6% to ₹158.4 cr.

financial_highlights.metric: Total income excluding FX and one-time items
PBT excluding FX and one-time items
FX gain/loss and one-time items in Q1 FY26 vs Q1 FY27
financial_highlights.value: Q1 FY26: FX gain ~₹39 crore plus one-time income ₹4.7 crore; Q1 FY27: FX loss ₹1.98 crore and one-time income ₹1.2 crore

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Sales of ₹158.4 crore, up 15.6% YoY; highest-ever monthly aftermarket sale of ₹63.06 crore in June 2026. New launches under SPARK include Disc Brake Rotors, TRW products, Clutch Master Cylinders, CV Brake Pads, Hydraulic Steering Systems and trailer Quick Fittings.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue of ₹271.4 crore, up 9.7% YoY, led by Double Diaphragm Spring Brake actuators, Uni-Stop Disc and CAM Brake Chambers, and Air Compressors; Uni-Stop Disc Brake Chamber ramp-up for North American customers. Growth came from the Chennai SEZ plant per management.

segments.name: Domestic CV >6T (OE)
segments.commentary: Sales grew 8.6% YoY versus industry CV >6T growth of 8.4%; management cited new product realisations (Exhaust Brake Valve, ECAS variants) and higher e-compressor penetration.

segments.name: Engineering services exports
segments.commentary: Growth of 12.5% YoY, driven by expansion of engineering activities delivered from India to global centres; services growth running at about 7.5% QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will ESC addressable market extend across CV segments including LCV, and will 12V content differ from 24V?
qa_highlights.answer: Shankar Venkatachalam said the ESC win is pneumatic ESC only; 12V is mostly intermediate CVs, and content per vehicle stays the same. LCV focus is on hydraulic ESC (already in series supply for some OEMs) and booster/tandem master cylinders.

qa_highlights.question: Will ZF's ESC market share mirror its pneumatic braking share, and will AEBS/ADAS also be won?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to retain its majority position across ABS plus ESC with most major OEMs. AEBS/ADAS is seen as separable with many standalone suppliers; ZF is nominated with some e-bus makers for EBS plus ESC full suite.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESC localisation level and when does manufacturing start?
qa_highlights.answer: Localisation is about 40-50% today, moving above 75% by SOP; manufacturing starts in Q3 of next year with local EMS partners.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook and order book for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Momentum is returning, driven by North American actuation products and air compressors from the Chennai SEZ plant; no quantified double-digit guidance given due to geopolitical uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic OEM growth and US/Europe market trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic CV growth was 8.6% in the quarter versus vehicle growth around 8.5%; US and Europe markets each declined about 10%, with US the larger decline, but ZF overall export sales were better.

qa_highlights.question: What were the headwinds and the base-quarter one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Headwinds were aluminium and gas price spikes, oil-linked consumables and chemicals costs, plus blue-collar shortages. The base quarter had about ₹39 crore FX gain (billing at 1.08x) plus actuarial one-timers, totalling ₹43.7 crore, versus ₹1.98 crore FX loss now.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost and other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited increments; ~₹8.4 crore employee cost recovery is offset by ₹8.5 crore recovery shown elsewhere, net ~₹17 crore India cost increase. QoQ other expenses rose ~₹12.4 crore from FX loss, CSR, consultancy/IT, director commission and service-location rent.

guidance_outlook: Management expects services growth to remain around the current ~7.5% level in coming months, supported by vehicle solutions, integrated brake controls, operations and performance improvement, advanced products and cybersecurity services.
Management declined to give a numeric export growth guidance for FY27 citing geopolitical uncertainty, but said outlook looks positive with a strong rebound expected in the US and Europe.
ESC manufacturing to start in Q3 of next year (FY28 per the call's timing); localisation at ~40-50% currently, expected to exceed 75% by SOP.

Commodity and FX cost pass-through: part recovered, balance under active discussion with OEMs; recovery typically has a two-quarter lag but has taken longer due to the West Asia conflict; expected to be secured over the next quarter.
Selective aftermarket price increases effective July 2026; PERFORM26 initiative targets CIS, productivity, value engineering and material cost optimisation.
Early Q2 signs: July 2026 vehicle production averaging 40,000-42,000 units, about 10,000 above a typical July; August and September seen at similar levels.
capex_capacity: New assembly lines for ASP cartridges and vacuum pumps productionised at the Oragadam multi-divisional facility; e-compressor and brake signal transmitter production scaled up.
New assembly lines for brake actuators and valves commissioned across the manufacturing network; strategic investments at Jamshedpur, Lucknow and Pantnagar improved flexibility.
Lucknow plant commissioned a 2,100 kilolitre rainwater harvesting system; Ambattur plant moved from LPG cooking to electric induction (about 16 tons LPG saved annually).
ESC homologation testing commenced for multiple customers at the ZF Proving Ground; Hemi Anechoic Chamber at ZF Test Track received NABL accreditation.
demand_pricing: Industry CV >6T production grew 8.4% in Q1 FY27; trailer market demand fell about 9% on slower mining, monsoon disruption and higher input costs.
Blue-collar manpower shortage across India in April and May affected industry production.
Aluminium rose from around ₹260/kg to over ₹360/kg per management; about ₹25/kg has come off since July, with easing expected if geopolitical tensions ease.
US and European markets each declined roughly 10% YoY per management, with US declining more; US market now ramping up.
ESC: business nominations secured from three major OEMs; management says ZF will retain majority position in ABS plus ESC market; content per vehicle unchanged across 12V and 24V.
EV bus sales reached 1,417 units in the quarter per management.
risks_watch: Commodity and FX cost pass-through from OEMs: partial recovery so far, balance still under negotiation; margin pressure from aluminium, chemicals and energy costs.
FX volatility: Q1 FY27 carried a ₹1.98 crore FX loss versus a large prior-year FX gain, so reported PAT is sensitive to FX items.
Geopolitical uncertainty affecting US/European export recovery and commodity prices; management declined to quantify export growth for FY27.
ESC ramp: manufacturing starting Q3 of next year, localisation must rise from 40-50% to above 75% by SOP; AEBS/ADAS nominations unconfirmed.
Trailer segment weakness (about 9% market decline) and labour shortages; monsoon-driven volume dip expected in July-September, though early July data looked stronger.
Leadership change: CFO Sweta Agarwal replaced by Rakesh Mishra effective September 1, 2026.
key_quotes: Despite these headwinds, we are at par with the market, supported by improved realizations from new product introductions such as the Exhaust Brake Valve and ECAS variants, along with increased market penetration of our e-compressor solutions.
The Aftermarket business delivered a strong performance in Q1 FY26-27, with sales of ₹158.4 crore, representing a 15.6% year-on-year growth.

Excluding the impact of foreign exchange (FX) gains/losses and one-time items, (₹43.7 crores) Profit before tax stood at ₹140.8 crores in Q1 2026-27, representing a strong 16.9% growth compared to Q1 of the previous financial year.

533033|2026-03.headline: ISGEC FY26 standalone revenue rose 4.2% to INR5,229 crore, below 7-8% guidance; FY27 revenue guided up 10-12%.

FY26 standalone PBT was INR455 crore (up 17%), of which about INR80 crore came from Philippines items that management classed as non-operational, leaving underlying operational PBT near INR375 crore. Consolidated PAT fell 25% to INR154 crore, driven by a catch-up depreciation charge after the Philippines business was reclassified from held-for-sale to continuing operations. Net borrowings fell to INR476 crore from INR836 crore.

533033|2026-06.headline: ISGEC Q1 FY27 standalone total income up 51% to INR 1,585 crore, but PBT up only 10% to INR 123 crore; FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%.
533033|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 51% YoY to INR 1,585 crore and EBIT grew 15% to INR 157 crore, with PBT up 10% to INR 123 crore as Q1 FY26 had high forex-driven other income. Manufacturing EBIT margin was 12% and projects EBIT margin 5.25%. Consolidated PBT was INR 53 crore, held back by an INR 83 crore loss at the Philippines ethanol plant, which ran at about 65-70% utilisation. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 10-12% and said it is conservative, citing carry-forward of order execution into FY28.

segments.commentary: Income up on improved execution per schedule; management expects roughly INR 1,000 crore per quarter in Q2 FY27 and projects EBIT margin of 5-6% for FY27. Export orders booked in Africa and Latin America.

segments.name: Manufacturing (standalone)
segments.commentary: Income lifted by dispatch of a roughly INR 130 crore US order that had been on hold; EBIT margin 12%, guided 12-13%. Steady-state consolidated manufacturing revenue guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen
segments.commentary: Orders in hand INR 889 crore. FY26 revenue about INR 670 crore; management expects about 10% growth in revenue and profit in FY27.

segments.commentary: Revenue down due to lower cane availability last season (untimely rain); cane availability improvement steps under way for next season.

segments.commentary: Q1 loss INR 83 crore at about 65-70% utilisation; crushed about 84,000 tonnes of cane, sold over 8 million litres of ethanol. Management targets about 90% utilisation by December and a much lower loss in Q2.

segments.commentary: Eagle Press about INR 150 crore a year; Isgec Titan Metal expected at about INR 150 crore in FY27 vs INR 102 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 top-line guidance only 10-12% despite strong execution and a larger order book, and what is the quarterly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a good part of order execution carries forward into FY28, which is why guidance is 10-12%. Projects are expected at about INR 1,000 crore a quarter and standalone manufacturing at a similar level in Q2 FY27, with Isgec Hitachi Zosen about 10% higher than FY26's roughly INR 670 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state manufacturing revenue on a consolidated basis, and how big was the Q1 US order?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated manufacturing was about INR 800 crore in Q1 and is guided at INR 750 crore plus per quarter for the next quarter, rising a bit later. The delayed US order was about INR 130 crore; the customer had paid 95% two or three quarters earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance conservative when Q1 alone adds about INR 570 crore of incremental revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers a conservative guidance it can meet over an aggressive one. It agreed the numbers could be higher and said there is hope for better outcomes.
